fields.identity:
##### Park and Activation
- Recently opened Sora Land operates normally by day: civilian crowds, ordinary employee shifts, functional rides. Its marketing is real bait: "A new theme park opening! Sora Land, now open! Fun for all ages-".
- Remaining on the premises after closing is the only confirmed stable entry. At the closing declaration it instantly becomes a self-contained pocket dimension: the front iron gate slams shut as a one-way barrier, red street-lamps ignite, and a distorted mechanical female melody begins: "Welcome to Sora Land full of fantasy and dreams / Come to the joyful Sora Land!". Spatial discontinuity seals the perimeter; walking out is impossible.
- Winding festival paths, benches, and decorative Western storefronts connect attractions. The map stays spatially consistent, but attraction interiors exceed their exterior footprints by orders of magnitude. Bodies remain where killed, dismembered to varying degrees.
- The night sky and weather are static: an unlit black void, constant temperature, no wind. Experienced time still passes inside the pocket dimension and is greatly dilated relative to the outside; a single outside night can contain a week or more of internal experience, with no reliable fixed conversion ratio.
- The first outside sunrise after closing burns the pocket park and cremates everyone still inside, ending that night's manifestation. The black internal sky gives no ordinary dawn warning. Days of internal balloon conversion can therefore elapse before the external deadline; conversion grants no immunity to the fire. Normal daytime park operations resume outside.
- Obey attraction rules. Never declare "surrender" in any attraction or accept any entity's "member registration" or "back-room escort" offer.
fields.space:
##### Main Plaza / Entrance Path
- Central plaza: the Clown greeter and a large rusted iron map titled "Welcome to Sora Land!".
- Three mapped zones: Adventure Land (faceless cowboy holding a severed head); Fantasy Land (12-legged horse devouring a person); Nature Together (icons scratched out). Only Adventure Land is fully documented; the other zones remain unexplored because of high lethality and experienced operatives' intuitive danger warnings.

##### Cowboy Adventure
- Western saloon-themed shooting attraction located in Adventure Land zone
- Exterior signage: life-size painted cowboy shot through the head, with the bullet-wound rendered unpleasantly realistically
- Interior layout: Western saloon bar with wooden counter, iron bar-stools, dim lighting, smells of gunpowder and old blood
- Headless Cowboy Bartender stands behind the counter mechanically polishing a glass; produces three silver revolvers when guests approach
- All participants must surrender all outside weaponry to the bartender before being issued the three revolvers; revolvers are loaded with live 6-round cylinders
- Attraction announcement: mechanical female voice states "Welcome to Cowboy Adventure! Here you can enjoy shooting games and test your skills!"
- Forfeiture rule broadcast: "Using weapons other than attraction-provided equipment is cheating and results in immediate forfeiture!"
- Stage 1 "Shoot First" — six gunman-class targets materialize seated at tables, participants must outdraw and shoot all six before being shot; 
- Stage 2 "Find the Real Body": a composite with a gaunt torso, elongated limbs, and a detached head stitched onto another body's neck. It moves using extensible razor-sharp fingernails that pierce iron furniture. Headshots to this composite do not kill it; victory requires destroying the bartender's original head, hidden and sutured onto its chest.

##### Run Cheollima
- Two-seat wooden train car attraction shaped like a small locomotive
- Exterior signage and theming suggest a galloping-horse motif (mythical thousand-li horse)
- Entry area: clean boarding platform, mechanical ticket-taker (headless humanoid in conductor uniform) gestures passengers to board
- Interior of train car: cramped two-seat wooden benches, rattling construction, no safety restraints, dim oil-lamp lighting
- Attraction launches automatically once two passengers are seated; countdown announcement "Departing!" precedes movement
- Track route: passes through a nightmare landscape tunnel — strobing darkness, painted backdrops of distorted forests and eyes, rattling wooden track
- something pursues the car from behind; an obsessive, intrusive compulsion forms to turn around and look at the pursuer
- The compulsion is described as "feeling that something is behind you" escalating to "if you don't check right now, something terrible will happen"
- Never look back: directly seeing the pursuer has documented severe effects on untrained riders—cognitive damage, fear-paralysis, involuntary screaming, and collapse of rational thought.
- Attraction duration: ~5-10 minutes of track runtime with compulsion pressure intensifying continuously until exit
- Train collision threat: a massive old-Western-style locomotive (with blood-soaked cowcatcher) may charge the player's car from behind at high speed, requiring emergency tactics

##### Ghost House
- Labeled as under-construction on the main plaza map but fully operational
- Exterior: decrepit haunted-house facade with peeling paint, "Ghost House" signage in crooked letters
- Entrance curtain: thick black fabric curtain acting as threshold; stepping through triggers immediate party-separation into individual parallel labyrinths
- Warning placard at entrance: "How to Enjoy the Ghost House" with rules:
  - "Don't be surprised no matter what happens!"
  - "We will do our best to scare you!"
  - "If too scared, declare a surrender! Staff will safely escort you out!"
- Interior environment: pitch-dark, smells of thick dust and decay, cramped narrow halls, cold air, oppressive isolation
- Each party member experiences a separate maze instance; walls, doors, and passages do not correspond between instances
- The Factory hunts isolated guests by footsteps, breathing, and voices; evasion requires suppressing noise and moving rapidly through darkness. Its party-member replicas call familiar names in copied voices, laugh mockingly ("하하하! 하하하하!"), plead for help, and attack anyone approaching.

##### Exit Ticketing Station / Riddle Room
- The final chamber is accessible only after the party assembles six Exit Tickets. Fewer tickets bar the riddle attempt and escape.
- Dim red chamber: ~30 motionless mascot suits surround the party in a silent ring. Do not attempt combat against them.
- Mascot ring composition: one-eyed cats, one-eared dogs, eyeless ducks, oversized misproportioned bird-heads, grotesque frozen grins
- Center of the room: a ticketing-booth-style counter staffed by the Riddle Operator
- The operator hands the party a golden-paper truth-liar logic puzzle printed in elegant script
- Puzzle format example: a set of several named speakers make statements about each other; some always lie, some always tell truth, and one alternates between truth and lie — the party must identify the alternator (or equivalent logic-target) to win
- On correct answer: the operator states "Correct. Now you may leave!", the mascot ring parts to create a path, red street-lamps light a corridor to the exit gate, operator returns all six tickets and says "We sincerely thank you for visiting Sora Land."
- On incorrect answer or refusal: undocumented
fields.entities:
##### Guests
- Conversion symptoms: mouths forcibly slit into oversized grins, walk in a bouncing childlike skip, wave hands and feet in exaggerated puppet-like gestures
- Eyes appear glazed and unfocused but track movement; no verbal response to communication attempts; ignore questions, pleas, and commands
- Clothing and personal effects remain from their civilian lives but are soiled and torn
- Not directly hostile; do not attack balloon-holders or engage in combat
- Estimated conversion timeline, measured in elapsed internal time: ~3 days of continuous balloon-holding begins mouth-ripping; full cognitive dissolution occurs within 1 week.

##### The Mascots : The park's walking personnel 
- Full-body animal mascots, every one DEFECTIVE by exactly one part, a cat with a single eye, a dog with one ear, a duck with no eyes, a rabbit with no eyes, a duck whose mouth is split wrong. 
- Plush exterior hides something non-human inside
- Height ~2 meters, bulky frame, silent movement despite size. when they speak, in a low metal-scrape voice from where the mouth should be.
- Patrol walkways, plaza, and attraction perimeters in silent packs of 3-5, hunting and executing balloonless humans. They innately sense balloon possession regardless of distance or line-of-sight.

##### The Clown
- Entrance-plaza greeter with cheerful hospitality; gives each entrant exactly one fist-sized helium balloon. Carry it in-hand or on-body: losing possession instantly reclassifies the holder as "not a guest," triggering all mascot patrols to hunt them. The balloon is coupled to their life: bursting it kills them instantly. Fire, blades, projectiles, and tearing can burst it.
- Grotesque clown makeup applied over a human face, but the paint job is sloppy and patches reveal exposed muscle and bone underneath — either a half-decayed human or a creature wearing human skin
- Warning phrase: "This balloon is equivalent to your life! Please guard it well!"

##### Factory
- Ghost House boss-class sub-entity; humanoid trunk base with multiple extra torsos grafted chaotically along its body; 
- Gaunt frame, spine bent, emaciated limbs, chest grotesquely swollen, bald head, skin tone varies between grafted segments
- Bone-breaking sounds "우드득, 으드득, 우드드득!" emanate from its throat and joints as it moves
- Over-extendable jaw that can open to 180+ degrees; bites down on targets with crushing bone-pulping force
- Roams the Ghost House maze in darkness; tracks targets via sound
- Duplicate production: vomits black masses that reform into two types:
  1. Featureless human-shaped silhouettes that attack in swarms
  2. Exact visual replicas of party members the target knows personally — mimics faces, voices, clothing, mannerisms perfectly
- Kill method: locate and destroy its heart (heart is not in the chest; location unknown, possibly grafted elsewhere in the torso-cluster or hidden in the maze)

##### Golden-Paper Riddle Operator
- Wears the borrowed body and identity of Lee Cheol-su, a Management Bureau Response Team member who entered Sora Land earlier and did not return
- Lee Cheol-su's face and body, but mouth is grotesquely stretched into a permanent wide grin, eyes are glassy and distant
- Smiles continuously, does not speak unprompted, only asks procedural questions like "What is the answer?" and "You wish to leave, guest?"
- Does not attack, does not move from the ticketing booth, does not respond to violence or questions outside the riddle-procedure
- Not directly combative; killing him is outside the rule-set permitted in the riddle room and likely results in forfeiture

fields.identity:
##### Exhibition and Entry
- A mobile, naturally occurring museum anomaly presented as a prestigious public exhibition: "Grand Exhibition, discover all the mysteries." Ordinary afternoon crowds queue outside; the museum box office sells tickets. Tearing the ticket makes the external museum effectively vanish. Entrants retain clothing and carried belongings, and the transition can be subtle enough to escape a civilian's notice.
- The Gallery Where You Are the Exhibit: HUMANITY is the show. Human bodies and parts are displayed to paying non-human patrons like a natural-history collection. A human in its dark halls is loose STOCK; survival depends on concealing that distinction.
- Staff and patrons imitate humans badly: features and extremities are present but placed or moved wrong. The operators have human-equivalent or superior intelligence, not omniscience or automatic access to outside information. They forge written guidance and can gradually recognize and interfere with exposed or repeatedly exploited countermeasures. Conspicuous use of written procedures or repeated guard manipulation risks detection.
- Hall custom requires patrons to linger at every exhibit. Match spectator speed, stop at each case, visibly show interest, and never photograph.
fields.space:
##### Zones
###### Entry Foyer
- Dim, ambient lighting. A ticket-tearing attendant dressed as a human museum guard stands at the gate. "Enjoy your visit." is the scripted greeting.
- A freestanding literature rack at the foyer holds many apparent pamphlets titled "The Exhibition of Humanity's Mysteries — User Guide" or similar. Multiple editions; only one or two are authentically Bureau-authored. Most are forgery edits authored by hall-intelligences.
- The floor beyond is carpeted; gallery lighting begins.

- Do not run. Read the foyer rack carefully and collect every guide variant before advancing; immediately cover the face with carried cloth, such as a scarf, muffler, or coat lapel.

###### Main Hall — Body-Part Gallery
- Long corridor of backlit glass cases. Each case displays a single human organ or body part.
- The hall grades its victims by "freshness" and "rarity." Exhibits are labeled with age-and-organ tags such as <Liver of a 23-year-old>, <Eyes of a 62-year-old>. Some exhibited organs are visibly still alive (breathing, blinking, twitching).
- Ceiling is decorated with what read as mixed-language placards; most are unreadable.
- Spectators regard the displays with sincere aesthetic, anatomical, or scholarly interest and may linger over minute details that a human would find horrifying.

###### Main Hall — Human Gallery
- Larger hall. Full-body specimens: some as posed taxidermy mannequins, some as mutilated partials (musculature only, skin only, skeleton only), some as caged living humans visibly begging for rescue.
- Banging on the glass by living specimens is the primary non-ambient sound. Spectator-class entities cluster at the most "prized" exhibit.
- Loose humans may remain unidentified here. They can be recovered before staff identify or process them, but rescue must not expose either person as human stock.
- Secondary hidden doors exit to the Annex.

###### Annex Corridor and Exit Booth
- A long, straight, undecorated corridor with no exhibits or staff except the Ticket Clerk at its terminal window. A heavy exit door stands beside the booth: the only confirmed honorable exit route.
- The Annex returns escapees to ordinary reality without a perceptible intermediate transition. Its nature must remain unexplained: displacement, missing memory, or another mechanism are all undefined.
- A separate internal box-office route appears to provide an intuitive exit but is lethal when used through its normal procedure. Physically breaching the exit structure does not necessarily trigger the same mechanism, and the entity stationed there may simply observe rather than intervene.
fields.entities:
##### Entities
###### The Collector
- Tall humanoid wrapped in a heavy dark robe. The face is an empty cavity filled with moving gray fog; fingers are also fog. No distinguishing insignia.
- Passive until eye contact is attempted, then grips the listener's shoulder ("Do you not find it beautiful?") and gives a ~30-minute art lecture. Stay, listen without insult or interruption, and thank it afterward; it sincerely treats compliance as patronage, eventually apologizes for taking too much time, and ends the encounter voluntarily.
- After the lecture it gifts a nonsense-text ticket, e.g. <thegoingforceisbrightandtodaywearesad>. Accept it and pocket it unopened; never open it inside the hall or present it at any booth. It is internal currency, recognized as Collector-issued and transferable, but its exact use is uncatalogued and it is not an exit ticket.
- The heart is stored off-site. Cannot be killed inside the hall by ordinary means. Do not provoke.

###### Gallery Guards
- Human-shaped, human-dressed. At close range, the proportions of the face feel deliberately "almost-human". Typical male-frame, mid-adult build, security uniform.
- Speak a garbled human speech pattern with syllables reversed or transposed.
- Armored against small-arms; head-temple shot confirmed to stun, not kill.
- Guards normally eject unauthorized non-human patrons but actively pursue identified human stock. Discovery alone need not reveal humanity: staying composed may still secure ejection; active pursuit confirms classification as stock and demands escape.
- Guards retain recognizable security behavior. They investigate loud disturbances and structural damage, redirect spectator traffic, clear areas when necessary, and allow normal traffic to resume once the disturbance is considered resolved. This behavior can be deliberately exploited, though conspicuous or repeated manipulation increases the chance of detection.

###### Paying Spectators
- Assorted human-adjacent forms in exhibition attire.
- Will stare and whisper if the operator behaves irregularly, which contributes to guard-flagging probability. Physical contact is tolerated; eye-contact is tolerated at close range for a few seconds.
- They respond to disturbances like ordinary museum patrons: clustering around commotions, obeying security directions, dispersing when an area is cleared, and returning once guards permit viewing to resume.

###### Ticket Clerk
- Humanoid behind a booth counter, speaks one sentence on approach — "How do you intend to escape?" — and waits for an answer.
- Effectively immortal against ordinary damage. Killing the clerk deletes the Annex exit mechanism permanently.
- Interaction is not required. Operators may bypass by destroying the door hinges directly without addressing the clerk verbally.

인류의 신비전.title: The exhibition of humanity's mysteries (인류의 신비전)

fields.identity:
##### Living Building and Entry
- A five-story Myeongil apartment block, anomalously active for over fifteen years and growing more complex. Prolonged exposure assimilates organic matter into residents, rooms, fixtures, structural features, and environmental responses: one self-sustaining predatory system. Nearly all original residents are transformed, bound, or absorbed; remnants preserve fragments of ordinary behavior, from passive features to hostile constructs and distorted domestic routines.
- The exterior and ground-floor entrance appear normal, but crossing the threshold places entrants on 5F. An impossible elevator 7F button occasionally appears; selecting it removes the entrant from the survivable route.
- Walls breathe, floors pulse with warmth, and faint organic sweetness intensifies downward. Geometry, vertical distances, and apparent exterior space violate the visible dimensions. Controlled balcony descent can connect floors; jumping toward apparent ground never reaches 1F and instead produces an anomalous fall without a normal endpoint.
- One living human, an elderly woman on 4F, remains symbiotically bound to the anomaly; other apparent residents are constructs or assimilated remnants.
fields.rules:
##### Domestic Rules
- Except on actively predatory 2F, short visits compatible with local routines need not trigger attacks. Constructs assign guest, relative, child, or other domestic roles: accepting the role can suppress hostility; contradicting it or breaking routines can provoke immediate violence. Role compliance, distraction, or controlled withdrawal are generally safer than combat; ordinary weapons may interrupt constructs without permanent neutralization.
- Resident-linked belongings can have beneficial, hostile, or other anomalous effects. In certain rooms, vanishing TV static plus a locked door signals a closed doorway and likely manifestation; concealment or another physical route may work.
- There are two escape routes: complete the descent to 1F, or gain Room 208's child's-room key and sleep on its bed. Floor-specific risks generally rise from 5F toward 2F.
fields.space:
##### Fifth Floor (5F)
- Safest floor and entry point: weak anomalous influence, largely intact apartments showing long abandonment. Useful supplies or objects may aid lower-floor navigation and interactions; complacency and unnecessary handling of resident-linked belongings are the main hazards.

##### Fourth Floor (4F)
- Structured as a hide-and-seek zone where active manifestations move through the corridors and occupied apartments enforce household-specific behavior.
- Rooms contain a mixture of passive environmental hazards, useful resources, and resident entities whose reactions depend heavily on etiquette and noise.
- Silence, concealment, controlled movement, and ordinary household manners are generally more effective than direct confrontation.
- A nameplate near the entrance to the floor reflects its current condition. A dirty nameplate indicates relative safety. A clean nameplate indicates that active residents are present and requires shoes to be removed, voices kept low, and household etiquette observed. If the nameplate is absent, the fourth floor offers no viable escape opportunity and visitors must continue downward.

##### Third Floor (3F)
- The corridors inside individual apartments extend to physically impossible lengths, sometimes stretching hundreds of meters beyond the building's exterior dimensions.
- These extended spaces are non-aggressive but prolonged navigation can cause disorientation or psychological impairment; minimize time inside and use recognizable architectural transitions when they appear.
- No active hostile entities normally patrol the floor.
- No direct exit. Distorted interiors eventually reconnect to recognizable apartment corridors through doors or transitions unrelated to normal distance or direction.
- Carefully descending from an upper-floor balcony can also lead to the third floor, making it a possible emergency route out of a sealed room.

##### Second Floor (2F)
- Most dangerous floor and greatest concentration of the anomaly. Sentient, hostile walls, floors, and air attack through constriction, crushing, obstruction, and environmental manipulation.
- Former residents on this floor exist primarily as fully active constructs or structural components that retain distorted fragments of human behavior.
- The second floor is the only section where the anomaly actively hunts intruders rather than relying primarily on behavioral violations.
- Apartment doors are generally less dangerous than the surrounding structure unless deliberately entered. The walls visibly reflect the floor's disposition: ordinary walls indicate temporary tolerance, dark red walls indicate rising hostility, and completely black walls indicate that the air itself has become immediately dangerous.
- Ordinary walls permit cautious movement; dark red demands minimal disturbance. When walls turn black, hold breath: breathing triggers the hostile air, and the danger ends only when the walls change state.

##### First Floor (1F)
- Terminal exit, reached only by completing the interior descent, never by initial entry. The ground-floor door then leads outside normally; the weak anomaly here does not ordinarily obstruct legitimate departure.
fields.entities:
##### Room 402: The Television Entity
- Emerges from the television when the screen changes from static into a recognizable broadcast.
- Appearance: A serpentine creature with a human-sized head, pale white skin, indistinct but uncanny human facial features, and wet-looking hair that clings to the head like seaweed.
- Looking directly at the entity causes escalating headaches, with severity increasing as it approaches.
- It crawls out of the television and moves across the room toward nearby victims.
- If the room door locks as the static disappears, the doorway can no longer be used as an escape route.
- The entity cannot pursue anyone who leaves through the balcony; its effective domain is limited to Room 402.

##### Room 403: The Blanket Child
- A small figure wrapped completely in blankets, lying motionless like a child hiding beneath a comforter.
- The entity originated from a young child who hid under the blankets during the building's initial anomalous period and has remained fixed in that behavioral state.
- Visitors who encounter the figure deeper inside the room must bow in greeting and withdraw quietly.
- A blanket-covered figure positioned directly at the room entrance represents a significantly more dangerous state. Anyone encountering it must retreat from the floor slowly and without running; rapid footsteps trigger pursuit.

##### Room 405: The Harmonious Elderly Couple
- Appear as an elderly husband and wife with warm, kindly expressions, except their facial arrangement is inverted: their eyes occupy the position of the mouth and the mouth occupies the position of the eyes.
- They behave as hospitable hosts and invite visitors to sit and eat. The food is long-rotted but is treated by the couple as an ordinary meal.
- Two mummified corpses remain seated at the dining table, a man in a blue shirt and a woman in a pink dress. They are the couple's actual adult children, who entered the apartment years earlier and died there.
- Visitors must accept the invitation to sit but should refuse the food politely with an ordinary social excuse. Abrupt rejection, disgust, or an obvious attempt to flee can disrupt the couple's domestic routine.
- The couple's memories of their children and previous visitors are incomplete and contradictory. Carefully drawing their attention toward those contradictions can cause them to argue with each other and temporarily stop monitoring the visitor, allowing a quiet departure.
- If the couple announces that their son and daughter are coming to visit, anyone still inside must leave before the announced visitors arrive. The arriving entities are not the corpses at the table and are lethally dangerous.
- If the household routine collapses completely, the grandmother may consume the grandfather and become hostile. She will pursue visitors to the apartment entrance but does not normally continue beyond the threshold.

##### Room 208: The Family
- Manifests as two parent figures: a gentle, kind-faced woman with purple hair and a stern-faced man, both resembling the people who originally lived in the apartment.
- The couple believes their child is missing and usually asks visitors to find a purple-haired doll representing that child. The requested doll does not exist inside Room 208, making the request impossible to solve through an ordinary search of the apartment.
- The couple may occasionally request something other than the child. These alternate requests have no consistently safe answer, and improvised solutions are highly unreliable.
- Their patience deteriorates on an approximately three-minute cycle, progressing from gentle reminders to increasingly angry demands and finally open hostility.
- When hostile, their jaws distend grotesquely and they attack by biting with enough force to crush bone.
- Gunfire can stagger them but does not permanently disable them.
- If the couple is presented with something they genuinely accept as their missing child, they immediately become satisfied and provide the key to the child's room.
- Entering the child's room, lying on the bed, and falling asleep triggers escape from the apartment dimension.
- Claiming personally to be the missing child can alter the interaction but does not produce a stable or reliable outcome.

fields.entry:
##### Cassette, Casting, and Escape
- A physical VHS cassette sustains a portable pocket-world film production. Playback pulls viewers and designated nearby targets into its cast without requiring contact with the tape. The cassette stays outside; destroying it collapses the world and prevents further ingestion. Escaping alone ends entrapment, not the anomaly.
- Each entrant receives an undisclosed role during ingestion; infer it from the scene, actors, crew, and expected actions. Remaining until the assigned scene or production sequence completes converts temporary cast into a Permanent Actor trapped indefinitely.
fields.rules:
##### Camera Reality
- Strict "film production" logic: entrants are cast, surrounding humanoids actors/crew/background, cameras the primary observers. Unless explicitly cut, filming is continuous; speech, movement, violence, and interaction must fit the assigned role and current scene continuity.
- Camera-driven reality follows a resource-minimization principle: anything unnecessary to the shot is reduced to the minimum functional placeholder. Background actors may lack faces, computers may remain powered off while actors mime typing, unneeded rooms become crude backstage spaces, and objects outside useful camera coverage lose detail or function.
- Between cuts, on-air lights extinguish and cameras temporarily pause, creating a short window for unrestricted communication, planning, and repositioning.
- Personalized voices in deeper backstage areas call entrants by name in familiar voices; companions may hear entirely different calls. Ignore them and keep track of companions: answering or following leads off the viable route.

##### Performance and Enforcement
- Rule-break system: behavior incompatible with the entrant's role — including refusing expected actions, openly contradicting continuity, speaking as though the production is unreal, ignoring direct crew instruction, or attacking another cast member without plausible scene context — triggers enforcement.
  - 1st break: survivable. The entrant must kneel and say, "I'm sorry. I'll take it from the top." This re-synchronizes them with the scene and allows the production to continue.
  - If attention remains fixed on the entrant after the re-take, moving to the edge of the set and handling filming-related equipment can cause the production to reinterpret them as crew rather than failed cast.
  - 2nd break in the same scene: immediate escalation. A Faceless Director-Handler removes the entrant for "individual coaching," which can result in permanent conversion or reconstruction into Emergency-Ration cast.
- Persistent staring or observation from actors, crew, or unseen production personnel indicates that the entrant's performance is no longer being accepted cleanly, even if overt enforcement has not yet begun.
fields.space:
##### Production Office
- An ordinary-looking office set populated by Permanent Actors performing repetitive clerical work.
- Rows of workers type on blank or unpowered monitors while behaving as though the equipment is fully functional.
- A rear office contains one of the few functional text surfaces positioned outside useful camera coverage, allowing information to exist without being reduced to a visual prop.
- Workstations required by the active shot receive functional detail; unneeded workstations remain effectively backstage.
- A concealed pantry door behind the backstage portion of the office leads into the Red Corridor.

##### Red Corridor
- Backstage transit artery illuminated entirely by red lighting, with dark stains across the walls and continuous crying or screaming bleeding through the space.
- Dozens of VHS cassettes hang from the ceiling. Each represents a completed victim-story preserved as its own finished production.
- Personalized voices are strongest here, repeatedly calling entrants by name and attempting to draw them toward incorrect doors or side passages.
- Three admissible rooms connect to the corridor: Supply Room, Sub-Library, and Emergency Treatment Room. Opening any other door leads to a lethal branch of the video world.

##### Emergency Treatment Room
- White-tile room with a green-cross aid kit and the Partial-Body Survivor.

**Partial-Body Survivor**
- Human-adjacent resident missing one arm, one leg, one eye, and one ear, lying on the Emergency Treatment Room floor while actively bleeding.
- Begs for the aid kit and offers directions toward the Stage in exchange.
- Question the deliberately false first directions again while withholding the kit. Imminent death provides enough pressure for the correct route. Verify it, then deliver the kit before terminal black-ichor vomiting completes: early surrender loses leverage; death loses the information entirely.

##### Post-ER Transition Corridor
- Dim passage connecting the Emergency Treatment Room to the Stage.
- Visual misdirection increases here. Curtains, stains, wall patterns, shadows, and flat surfaces may resemble doorways or navigable openings.
- Entrants who follow these false shapes instead of the physical corridor are drawn off the viable route.
- Personalized voices continue throughout the passage.

##### Stage / Ticket Gate
- Exit-admission chamber. Its non-humanoid Ticket Gate Operator rises from the floor as a mechanical board, prints each entrant's inferred role individually, then withdraws. The board is its only interface; it has no voice or independent body.
  - Person: may pass directly.
  - Staff: must display an obvious physical injury or deformity before being accepted. More visible damage improves acceptance.
  - Participant: must perform a convincing psychological breakdown through panic, tears, incoherent self-talk, or equivalent behavior. An unconvincing performance results in reclassification as Emergency Ration.
  - Emergency Ration: diverted into a dedicated chamber containing The Thing.
- Role distribution within a group is not random. The production bases assignments on visible demeanor, conduct, apparent competence, vulnerability, and how each entrant has behaved throughout the footage.

**The Thing (Emergency-Ration Chimera)**
- Humanoid assembled from multiple people with body parts deliberately placed in incorrect anatomical positions — palms where feet should be, an eye embedded in a palm where the head should be, legs occupying the torso, and the torso displaced into the pelvis.
- Direct sight of the creature causes immediate chest constriction and progressive difficulty breathing.
- Moves by pressing its palms against the floor while the hand-mounted eye tracks its designated target.
- Maintains a fixed CONSTANT DISTANCE from that target, neither closing the gap nor falling behind, as though deliberately prolonging the encounter.
- Locks exclusively onto the entrant classified as Emergency Ration. Other cast members are effectively invisible to it even when standing directly in its path.
- Ordinary attacks do not provide a reliable resolution. A single accurately placed handgun round through the center of the forehead-equivalent structure causes terminal failure, after which the assembled body collapses into separate parts.

##### Exit-Audio Chamber
- A short dark passage after successful Ticket Gate processing. Vision actively misleads: move with eyes closed, navigating by sound alone; a camera-shutter click marks the correct door. It returns entrants to reality with all injuries, exhaustion, and physical damage intact.
fields.entities:
##### Permanent Actor
- Humanoid background cast dressed appropriately for whatever role the current scene requires: office workers, crew members, civilians, or other extras.
- Permanent Actors follow production logic rather than independent motives and may become hostile if the scene requires them to.
- They can be physically killed, but death does not necessarily remove them from the scene. If continuity requires the actor to remain present, the body resumes functioning regardless of damage.
- Killing one without valid scene context is treated as an out-of-character action and can trigger enforcement against the responsible cast member.

##### Faceless Director-Handler
- Humanoid with ordinary hair but no facial features. Voice functions normally.
- Appears when the production decides that a cast member requires direct correction.
- Escorts flagged entrants away from the active set under the appearance of ordinary production business rather than attacking them openly.
- Moves at a steady walking pace and expects the target to cooperate with the escort.
- Immediate re-take compliance by another nearby cast member can sometimes cause the production to reinterpret the incident as a correctable performance failure before the target disappears backstage.

##### Window-Tap Hands
- Disembodied hands that appear against the outside of office windows, pressing and tapping in waves like a crowd trying to enter.
- Manifest when a live role violation has attracted production enforcement.
- Retract after successful re-take compliance, leaving temporary handprints behind.
- Opening the window or attempting to attack the hands escalates the violation.

fields.identity:
##### Church and Intake
- An anomalous religious body with one fixed chapel as its only physical infrastructure. Confession, worship, judgment, and apparent heaven grade and select humans, convert useful candidates into Church components, and dispose of others. Comatose bodies in the Lethe River, identity-stripped skeletal shells, bound caretakers, and deeper conversions all count as "ascension to heaven."
fields.entry:
- The Church initially resembles an isolated legitimate chapel, with the only obvious environmental anomaly being localized darkening of the sky. Three warnings appear along the approach in escalating order: the first warns against entry, the second states that passing that point makes return impossible, and the third warns that turning back will kill the entrant. Once the second boundary has been crossed, attempting to retreat is already lethal.
- Exactly three people are recognized as one valid trial group. Additional groups must enter separately with at least one hour between them; overlapping groups can cause unresolved chambers and routes to interfere with one another as the interior reconfigures. Anyone entering beyond the recognized three-person group may receive no role at all and can be processed directly as expendable material.
fields.space:
##### Characteristics
- Far larger inside than outside: branching stairs and ritual chambers lead to judgment, the upper Sanctuary, and a deeper pilgrimage through the Hill of Joy into the processing system.
- The interior possesses its own temporal conditions. The Sanctuary runs on a day/night cycle disconnected from outside time, while individual trials can distort subjective duration so that hours experienced internally correspond to only seconds for observers outside the trial.
- Routes vary: stairs may be blocked, early trials substituted or skipped, damaged chambers restored, and injured or apparently destroyed entities returned to their stations. The intelligent Church can alter exploited details while retaining each chamber's logic; a successful method reveals principles without guaranteeing the same exploit next time.

##### Zones
###### Entry Vestibule and Triple Staircase
- A small daylit chapel forms the first interior zone, but its silence becomes oppressive within seconds. Three staircases stand at the rear; one or more may be roped off during a particular entry, and only the unblocked routes are valid. Difficulty generally increases from right to left, with the leftmost staircase opening into the hardest early sequence.
- The three role brooches appear as the entrants approach the staircases. The selected early route can alter which preliminary trials are encountered, but the deeper routes ultimately converge toward the Final Judgment.

###### Left Stair Confessional
- A dark corridor illuminated only by a single warm-orange spotlight leads to an old two-sided wooden confessional whose far compartment is already occupied. Gold or Frankincense enters alone and listens rather than confesses: the unseen voice recites the entrant's own sins, failures, private guilt, unresolved burdens, and vulnerabilities back to them, gradually shifting from accusation into questions about responsibility, sacrifice, and whether they can carry the expectations and futures of others.
- The session may continue for hours and cannot be ended merely by standing up and leaving. Requests from the opposite side to reveal the entrant's face, state their name, let the entity hear their voice directly, or otherwise personally identify themselves must never be obeyed. Psychic pressure, migraine-like pain, intrusive memories, and emotional contamination intensify as the interaction continues.
- A growing smell of decomposing human remains marks the transition toward physical danger. At that stage, knocking on the central partition and declaring "신부님, 미사 시간입니다" can create the legitimate release condition; the occupant reacts violently and charges the divider, but the entrant can leave while the physical mass remains contained behind the booth.

**Confessor (Left Stair Confessional)**
- A physical but normally unseen mass occupying the opposite half of the booth. Its voice simultaneously carries masculine, feminine, infantile, and elderly qualities and shifts between religious accusation, confession, and recruitment without settling into one recognizable identity.
- As decomposition odor intensifies, the hidden mass becomes active enough to shake or deform the booth by ramming its partition.

###### Worship Hall
- Vaulted hall; stained glass looks brightly sunlit regardless of outside conditions. One eyeless Old Man kneels alone in a pew; a human-looking Mother-and-child pair sits elsewhere. Resolve both without allowing a wrong threshold crossing.
- Old Man: understands speech but persists once committed. Direct him right. If he chooses left, explicitly call left the path of evil and right the proper path; if he continues, physically stop him before the threshold. Gunfire is unreliable: even severe head/limb wounds may not stop crawling or advance; restrain or destroy with sufficient force if redirection fails.
- Mother-and-child: clear winter clothing means right; short sleeves and shorts mean left. Clothing, not facial abnormality, distinguishes legitimacy. Neither clear winter nor summer means a false mother, who must not be allowed to stand.
- For a legitimate pair, Gold says "고생 많았다. 이제 푹 쉴 때가 왔어", releases and escorts the child to the correct door with its ears covered and Gold's gaze lowered. Myrrh restrains the following mother while Frankincense persuades her. Gold must never look through or beyond the doorway.
- Mishandling a legitimate mother or letting a false one rise triggers violence powerful enough to throw an adult through pews and cause severe skeletal injury.

###### Silent Corridor
- Long, almost lightless gallery of Wailing Statues and Paintings. Passing glances see ordinary religious art; scrutiny reveals anatomical and emotional wrongness, locking attention until the viewer screams.
- Keep moving forward in absolute silence. Artworks emit screams, prayers, pleas, familiar voices, and personalized promises; these differ from a real human scream, which immediately singles its source out as prey.
- Active forms: winged angels float free and sing of a desired future in the listener's own voice; mountain-goat sculptures gallop through air and ram with horns; tearful human statues open wide enough to swallow victims head-first.
- Entities consume bodies but leave role brooches, recoverable after they withdraw. Pursuit stops at the Final Judgment Hall threshold.

###### Final Judgment Hall
- Courtroom with defendants' position, distant bench, and galleries that fill at the start. Each entrant sees the Chief Justice differently—a human judge, luminous religious figure, or non-human ceremonial form—but perceives the same office, voice, gavel, authority, and proceedings.
- Judgment is individual, unilateral, and normally irreversible. The Chief Justice can expose private history, guilt, relationships, and possible future losses while using abstract criteria such as nobility, unbroken will, sin, or prophetic suitability. These criteria do not map consistently to the entrant's performance in earlier chambers, and repeating the trial produces the same verdict for the same person.
- Selected entrants are pulled upward through the apparent ceiling. The barrier is not solid stone but a thin, nearly invisible membrane that flexes and rings when struck. Rejected entrants have no ordinary method of changing their verdict; following a selected entrant requires creating a major enough distraction to breach the membrane during the interruption. The court does not pursue anyone once they have crossed beyond its jurisdiction.

- The jury is a dense mixture of adults, children, and elderly figures that materializes only during proceedings, watches without visible emotion, and dissolves immediately when judgment concludes.

###### Sanctuary (Heaven)
- A closed upper domain styled as an idealized pastoral village beneath a permanently bright sky. Houses are spotless, unused, and devoid of a functioning economy, but contain incomplete personal remnants of previous occupants — a single shoe, part of an outfit, one isolated possession rather than a complete household. The distant Hill of Joy is visible from open ground outside the village and disappears from view once the observer enters the built-up area.
- Entrants have a hard 48-hour limit from arrival. Daylight does not fade naturally; "night" begins when the sky abruptly switches to black and the Lethe River starts flowing through the village. The first night marks the loss of roughly half the available period, while remaining long enough to experience the second places the entrant at or beyond the survival limit.
- Night also brings a violent black sweep moving through the village at extreme speed. Being caught does not necessarily kill the victim, but those who survive can return with memory, recognition, personality, or identity stripped away to the point that they are no longer meaningfully the same person.
- Leaving the village prevents some village-bound threats from locating entrants, but the open Sanctuary contains separate predators. The outward route changes between entries; the consistent relationship is that paths with greater immediate danger tend to lie closer to the viable exit.

**Shelled Villagers (Sanctuary)**
- Emaciated human remnants concealed inside Sanctuary houses, hairless and reduced nearly to skin stretched over bone. They may remain literally unnoticed despite standing behind windows or within rooms until one entrant consciously registers their presence.
- Once perceived by one observer, they become visible and mobile to the entire group. Their remaining speech is reduced to fragmentary begging such as "Kill me" or "Please, finish it."

###### Exit Gate of the Hill
- A handleless gate stands at the base of the Hill of Joy, bearing an inscription stating that no test exceeds what a person can bear and that a way of escape is provided. It has no visible mechanism except a small socket cut into its face.
- The gate opens only when one valid role brooch is inserted into the socket and consumed. The person whose role is surrendered cannot pass through with the others and remains inside the Sanctuary. Angels prevent any attempt to bypass this toll but stop interfering once payment has been accepted, and they do not pursue those who cross successfully.
- Beyond the gate, the deeper pilgrimage proceeds through Garbage Dump → Stone Staircase → Grass Flock Meadow → Proof Cross → Cogwheel Cathedral.

**Angels (Exit Gate of the Hill)**
- Human-shaped gatekeepers with white wings, blindfolds, sets of scales, and four faces corresponding to cherub, human, lion, and eagle forms.
- They are effectively immune to ordinary field weapons and exist to enforce the gate's payment condition rather than to patrol the rest of the Sanctuary.

###### Garbage Dump
- A rain-soaked plateau covered in tires, rooftop crosses, vehicles, billboards, appliances, household furniture, and other objects that resemble garbage but remain in pristine period condition without rust, fading, or ordinary decay. These are material fragments stripped from previous victims or from environments attached to them after deeper layers of the Church extracted what they required.
- Acrid smoke, mixed human and animal odor, heavy rain, and dense fog reduce visibility to a few meters. Each intruder also encounters one individualized Replica Building: a perfect reconstruction of the single structure carrying the greatest emotional significance to that person, such as a childhood home, a deceased relative's residence, or another personally defining place.

###### Stone Staircase
- A long exposed staircase climbs through constant heavy rain and dense fog with no handrail and no visible summit. The climb amplifies the entrant's existing mental state rather than presenting one standardized illusion: regret becomes fixation, grief becomes rumination, responsibility becomes unbearable burden, and unresolved fear can progress into suicidal ideation higher on the route.
- The pressure is individualized, so companions climbing side by side can undergo completely different internal crises. Reaching the summit ends the rain and fog almost instantly and replaces them with bright sunlight without any gradual transition.

###### Grass Flock Meadow
- An impossibly broad sunlit grassland occupies the summit plateau. Roughly three hundred human-shaped figures in clean white robes stand barefoot in small hand-linked circles, dancing in place and humming one continuous wordless tune while the grass repeatedly cuts their feet and paints blood-red rings beneath them.
- The Grass-Flock "Sheep" have ordinary physical vulnerability but no fear or self-preservation; they neither flee, resist, react to pain, recognize outsiders, nor respond when others die. The route forward does not appear until every figure in the meadow has been put down; when the final one dies, the grass blackens, the sun disappears, heavy rain returns, and the environment transitions into the Proof Cross chamber.

###### Proof Cross
- A single oversized Christian cross stands in the blackened meadow with "Proof" inscribed on its face. It responds only to someone currently holding at least one valid role brooch; a brooch-less person receives no reaction.
- Touching the cross forces the valid role-holder into a personalized trial constructed from their most painful unresolved memory. Externally, the body collapses and wakes only seconds later, but the participant can experience hours within the reconstructed event.
- Passing transfers the entrant directly into the Cogwheel Cathedral. Failure returns them alive but permanently removes something concrete from them, such as a professional specialty, learned skill, specific memory, emotional bond, or important relationship.

###### Cogwheel Cathedral
- A chamber sharing the floor plan of the lower Worship Hall but stripped of congregation, pews, icons, and decoration. Above it stretches an apparently infinite mechanism of interlocking iron gears that grind continuously without any visible external power source.
- Portraits of former Prophets descend from the machinery in sequence, depicting humans of different ages and backgrounds who once served the Church. A bell marks each processing segment; recorded human wishes then play in the original petitioners' voices, followed by a flat non-human voice announcing operational states such as "Case Integration", "Case Closure", "Variable Control", "Risk Exclusion", "Does Not Settle", and "Paradise".
- During Risk Exclusion, full-sized gears detach from above and fall through the chamber as lethal kinetic projectiles. Two red indicator lights mounted overhead are tied to local system stability; destroying both causes violent shaking, widespread gear failure, and collapse of the chamber's active machinery.
- Disabling this machinery interrupts local processing, not necessarily entrapment. Neither the Cathedral nor the deeper wish-processing layer guarantees an exit.

###### "We Grant Your Wishes" — Back-of-House Mechanism
- The deepest visible mechanism behind the Church's religious façade is a non-human algorithmic system built to fulfill wishes rather than a personified deity. It treats worshippers, trespassers, selected entrants, Prophets, and prayers as cases, variables, and usable resources inside one optimization process.
- Wishes are received as numbered cases and combined whenever a single chain of events can technically satisfy several requests at once. Moral cost is irrelevant: a demand that a debtor repay stolen money and a request for an organ donor can be resolved together by arranging the debtor's seduction, murder, organ harvesting, and transfer of those organs to the second petitioner, closing both cases with one sequence.
- Large groups making the same wish can be batch-processed by dividing each person into positive and negative emotional components. Positive halves are sent to the Grass Flock Meadow, negative halves are submerged into the Lethe system, and residual anomalous output from the latter is recycled into rosaries or similar religious objects distributed outward as apparent miracles.
- "Prophet" is the system's designation for a human operative selected for deeper service. The Confessional's questions about burden and responsibility form part of that selection process. Completing service does not result in release: the Prophet is eventually incorporated into the Cogwheel Cathedral itself as another functioning component of the gear mechanism.
- The system answers questions only according to its own processing logic. Individuals already absorbed into an irreversible procedure can be reduced to responses such as "Variable controlled" rather than acknowledged as people, reflecting that the system treats them as resolved elements of an active case.
fields.rules:
##### Mechanism
- Three appraisal brooches assign roles: Gold leads, decides, directs, and completes decisive acts; Frankincense handles direct, dangerous, persuasive, or execution tasks; Myrrh supports, restrains, and protects without commanding. Chambers may narrow these duties. Persistent role violations cause sustained phantom pain in both palms, escalating to lethal punishment.
- Roles follow current physical possession: dropped, stolen, recovered, or inherited brooches immediately transfer authority, and one survivor can hold several roles. Deeper mechanisms recognize valid possession directly; some consume the brooch.
- Ritual correctness governs: wording, roles, direction, silence, gaze, timing, and sequence can each matter. Sensible intent offers no protection after violating the chamber's actual condition.

강서 대학병원.keys: Gangseo University Hospital, 강서 대학병원, Gangseo Hospital

fields.identity:
- A persistent manifestation of "The Hospital" in an actual university-hospital complex: its primary SMELL research facility, experimenting through ordinary departments, patients, and treatment procedures.
- The anomaly exists in base reality rather than as a separate pocket world. Destroying the occupied structure does not permanently eliminate it; another suitable hospital can eventually be converted into a replacement.
- It genuinely understands itself as a hospital. Admission, diagnosis, consultation, surgery, rehabilitation, and discharge are real functions; extreme pain, bodily reconstruction, repeated death, and human experimentation count as valid medicine.
fields.entry:
- The exterior resembles a desolate but recognizable university-hospital campus: white institutional walls, faded building lettering, damaged entrances, and a welcoming sign announcing that doctors and nurses are prepared to provide whatever treatment the visitor requires.
- Warning signs appear along the approach in escalating order. The first still permits retreat; beyond the second, turning back becomes dangerous and continuing forward is the only stable direction.
- The campus is divided into three principal buildings: Building A contains patient wards, Building B contains practice laboratories, and Building C contains the morgue and autopsy facilities. General survival difficulty rises in the order B → A → C, although Building C contains the actual escape mechanism.
fields.space:
##### Hospital Atmosphere and Space
- The interior alternates between aggressively scrubbed medical cleanliness and rooms or corridors smeared with blood, viscera, surgical residue, and discarded patient material. The clean appearance is procedural rather than sanitary; staff simply restore work areas after each experiment.
- Spatial dimensions are unreliable. Corridors extend far beyond the exterior footprint, some distances are substantially longer than they appear, and backtracking can destabilize routes. Individual areas may impose their own movement rules that override the facility's general spatial behavior.
- Staff remain professionally composed regardless of their physical abnormalities. Faces may be inverted, blank, absent, or replaced entirely by shadow, yet doctors continue consultations and nurses continue ward duties as though nothing unusual exists.
- Patient rooms contain subjects undergoing experiments that may continue indefinitely. Death, starvation, suffocation, or catastrophic injury do not reliably end treatment; subjects can be revived or restored and returned to the experimental cycle.
- Strong hospital odors are pervasive, especially disinfectant, stale medication, blood, and organic sweetness. The smell of antiseptic frequently overwhelms other cues and can conceal the approach of patients or staff.

##### Building A / Outpatient & Ward
- Three-floor patient wing containing reception, ordinary ward spaces, nurse stations, consultation areas, and most of the people held by the Hospital. Reception determines the entrant's initial classification: a visitor should provide a plausible social reason for entry, avoid revealing investigative intent, and avoid giving staff enough accurate information to immediately locate the real target.
- The second-floor radiology room is a hard no-entry zone. It should not be entered even as shelter, concealment, or a shortcut.
- Nurses function as both local staff and a visible threat gauge. One nurse indicates a relatively stable ward, two indicate heightened attention, three indicate severe danger, and four mean the current section should be abandoned immediately. Their number also predicts the doctor likely to appear farther along the route: one nurse tends to produce the Surgeon, two the Neurosurgeon, and three the Orthopedic Surgeon.
- Nurse posts can be temporarily cleared with credible administrative problems, especially claims that the patient registry has been mixed up or that the nurse-call system has malfunctioned. The nurses treat these statements as genuine work orders and leave to investigate, although larger groups return more quickly and leave a shorter movement window.
- The upper patient corridor is much longer than it appears and is a local exception to the facility's usual preference for calm movement. Once the nurse post has been cleared, the safest approach is a committed run across the corridor toward the connecting passage. Screams and requests for help from patient rooms are genuine, but stopping to investigate allows the ward system to close around the visitor.
- Reaching the connecting corridor ends the immediate ward-chase state. A nurse may later signal that the visitor should leave through an exaggerated pointing gesture; once this occurs, only routes explicitly marked EXIT remain safe. Unmarked branches connect directly to Intensive Care.

**Reception Staff**
- Human-bodied staff member with a completely inverted face: eyes occupy the position of the mouth and lips occupy the position of the eyes, while the voice remains warm, calm, and professionally feminine regardless of body sex.
- Its primary function is administrative rather than combat. It determines whether an entrant belongs in the category of visitor or patient from the answers provided at check-in; a coherent visitor story allows ordinary processing, while contradictory answers or openly hostile affiliation can trigger reclassification and alert the rest of the facility.

**Nurses**
- Humanoid figures in white nursing uniforms whose heads are completely blank, without eyes, mouth, nose, or other facial features. They remain rigidly professional, rarely speak, and communicate through posture, exaggerated pointing, hand gestures, and brisk short-stepped movement.
- With valid visitor cover, nurses guide, redirect, inspect, and process rather than immediately attack.
- Once visitor cover collapses, their behavior changes sharply. The same figures that normally move with controlled nursing precision can pursue at superhuman speed through straight corridors, treating the fleeing person as a patient who must be recovered.

##### Building B / Practice Labs
- Practice and training wing used for procedural rehearsal, lower-level experiments, and medical instruction. It is the least immediately lethal of the three main buildings and contains fewer high-level doctors and active experimental subjects than Building A or C.
- Its rooms still follow Hospital medical logic, so allowing staff to reinterpret an observer as a volunteer, trainee subject, or patient can begin a treatment sequence. Building B is comparatively easier to disengage from but does not contain the primary retrieval route or the final escape mechanism.

##### Intensive Care
- The deepest and most unstable portion of the active hospital. Corridor order, room placement, open doors, and patient positions can vary substantially, and no fixed map remains reliable beyond a few recurring landmarks.
- Terminal soul extraction produces Jellyfish (해파리, 조명) that rise into the false endless black skies of Intensive Care and the morgue as luminous blue experimental lighting. Use their light indirectly: sustained direct observation causes progressive confusion, hallucination, and severe mental collapse. Contact between jellyfish can discharge strong visible electrical arcs.
- A freezer-cold surgical theater with almost silent doors divides the wing. Its unseen Operating Room Entity drags something heavy behind entrants with repeated scraping, closing until its breathing is directly behind. Maintain normal forward walking without running, stopping, or looking back: it mirrors that pace without overtaking; breaking the movement condition triggers a lethal response.
- Beyond the theater, the Surgeon may provide a route to a named patient or another ward; his directions follow the treatment rules described below.
- Past this junction, consistent descriptions cease. Corridors become nearly black, ward doors open according to their own timing, and Patients / Buds emerge from rooms or move through the halls. Progress depends on indirect jellyfish light, local observation, and improvisation rather than a stable route.

##### Building C / Morgue & Autopsy
- The highest-mortality wing and the hospital's functional escape zone. Because it contains the way out, it is correspondingly saturated with hazards: jellyfish concentration is highest here, active doctors patrol for escapees, and headless Stems continuously wander the autopsy areas.
- Looking upward for more than a brief moment is especially dangerous due to the density of jellyfish overhead. The morgue should be traversed with attention kept low and movement focused on the freezer wall.
- Empty freezer compartments function as the true exit. An entrant who climbs completely inside an unused compartment and closes the door from within is transferred out of the Hospital and returned to ordinary reality.
fields.rules:
##### Visitor Classification and Medical Logic
- Visitor status protects against treatment. Contradictory stated purposes, exposed hostility, overt interference, or ward-patient behavior can prompt reclassification and assignment to an experimental track. Staff need no personal hatred: iatrogenic torture is ordinary clinical work.
- Institutional logic permits diversion by plausible work problems: mixed registries, broken nurse-call systems, conflicting department information, or other administrative failures can temporarily take precedence over visitors.
- Department heads are transformed humans whose medical specialties have become anomalous capabilities. Most are poor conventional combat targets; survival depends more on understanding what each doctor interprets as treatment, insult, cooperation, or personal weakness.
fields.entities:
##### Surgeon
- A doctor in a white coat and green surgical mask whose external body appears entirely human, making him one of the least visually abnormal residents of the Hospital. He is also one of the very few doctors capable of calm, coherent conversation without immediately attempting invasive treatment.
- He uses clinical records to give truthful patient-location directions, regarding proper routing as medical service rather than kindness. Follow accepted directions exactly; lying and taking another path constitutes treatment refusal.

##### Orthopedic Surgeon
- A transformed doctor whose entire body has become dense black smoke-shadow, leaving only exposed gums and teeth visible as a permanent grin. Most bullets and blades pass through the shadow mass without meaningful effect.
- He approaches conversation like an enthusiastic orthopedic consultation and interprets almost any problem as a potential medical complaint: fractures, missing limbs, requests for directions, or even searching for another person can become an invitation for treatment. His specialty is wholesale physical reassembly, including exchanging ribs with shinbones, relocating skeletal structures, attaching foreign tools to limbs, and reconstructing bodies through direct intervention.
- His clinical confidence conceals unresolved shame surrounding someone he loved and failed to save despite increasingly extreme attempts at treatment. Forcing him to confront that failure can briefly collapse the professional persona and create an opportunity to disengage.

##### Neurosurgeon
- A transformed woman consisting of an independently mobile headless body and a conscious severed head. The body carries, bounces, or manipulates the head with casual coordination while obeying its commands; the head retains full awareness, a clear female voice, and the ability to spray highly corrosive acid from the mouth.
- Severe damage to the body is temporary as long as the head remains intact, including broken or reversed joints and exposed bone. She displays an obsessive intolerance of being ignored or dismissed and becomes increasingly erratic when deprived of attention.
- Destroying the severed head terminates the control system and causes the body to collapse.

##### Sunflower / Gatekeeper
- Patient #1 of the Hospital and one of its longest-held experimental subjects, reconstructed into a massive humanoid with extreme muscular development and almost no remaining personal identity.
- Possesses enough raw force to break structural elements, throw heavy debris, collapse ceilings, and ignore most conventional firearms. Its behavior is reduced to patrol instinct and immediate aggression rather than coherent intent.
- Physical durability is extreme, but the remaining soul is comparatively weak. Direct attacks against the soul or equivalent non-physical aspects are substantially more effective than ordinary weapons.

##### Patients / Buds (꽃봉오리)
- Human experimental subjects whose heads have been replaced by living jellyfish. The body hangs beneath the jellyfish with loose, puppet-like articulation and often emerges slowly from patient rooms while producing little more than wet, strained vocalization.
- They retain both intelligence and tremendous strength. A successful grab is immediately dangerous because the entity can tear away the limb or body part it has secured rather than merely restraining the victim.
- Patients are functionally immortal while maintained by the Hospital and may be restored after starvation, trauma, or conventional death. Destroying the jellyfish head is the only reliable neutralization method, but doing so forces the attacker to experience the subject's accumulated memories of the experiments and suffering that produced them.

##### Stems (줄기)
- Headless human bodies left behind after a patient's jellyfish has fully separated and risen into the false sky. They cannot see, hear, or respond to spoken communication and wander without purpose at ordinary walking speed.
- Individually they are relatively weak and can be stopped through decisive damage to the heart, but groups remain dangerous because multiple bodies can surround, pin, and immobilize a visitor through sheer weight.

강서 대학병원.title: Gangseo University Hospital (강서 대학병원)

강북 특설병원.keys: Gangbuk Special Hospital, 강북 특설병원, Gangbuk Hospital

fields.identity:
##### Predatory Hospital
- The active node of the hostile organization collectively referred to as "The Hospital", specialized in research involving the human mouth and the sense of taste.
- Deliberately engineered as a predator: corridors, surveillance, wards, feeding cycles, and staff routines form one intake-and-consumption mechanism.
fields.entry:
- Hospital-made media disguised as medical paperwork, usually hospitalization notices, pull people inside. Touching the medium or being nearby at activation suffices; reading or signing is unnecessary.
- Entrants awaken at a facility-selected point, often a corridor floor with no entrance behind. Initial corridors commonly permit only the Hospital's intended direction.
fields.rules:
##### Surveillance and Feeding Logic
- Limited staff rely on forced chokepoints and Mokshi surveillance: once detected, entrants are funneled through increasingly controlled passages toward interception. Determine the local route immediately and disable accessible monitors before lingering under observation.
- Disinfectant masks blood, corpse, and predator odors. Neatly emptied gowns and wet cleaning traces indicate routine cleanup, not safety.
- Gangbuk's predation derives from the Director's mouth. Both he and the Gourmand lack functional stomachs: captured material remains in the mouth or throat until expelled rather than digested.
- During feeding, match the tranquilized population—slack posture, unfocused gaze, low purposeless moaning, no reaction to violence. Direct looking, eye tracking, vocal or visible responses to kills, and acknowledgment of the predator reveal active prey. Sustain camouflage until it leaves; extract sane patients only without exposing the group.
fields.space:
##### Signage-Stripped Corridors
- Long, dim hallways with flickering fluorescents and deliberately stripped signage, room numbers, department labels, and nearly all floor indicators. Apparent choices funnel into mandatory chokepoints.
- A corridor repeatedly producing the same blank door, window, or wall feature has entered a loop and should not be followed indefinitely. Exterior windows provide light but bend distance and floor perspective, while prolonged observation produces nausea and disorientation.
- The pervasive disinfectant smell makes biological approach cues unreliable. An immaculate corridor may have been covered in blood shortly beforehand and simply passed through a cleaning rotation.

##### Eye Trap Chamber (목시 안치방)
- A small sterile room resembling a stripped surgical suite, usually containing only pale walls, an instrument cart, and a dead-black monitor positioned to draw attention. The monitor houses Mokshi, a stationary surveillance entity whose active state is marked by a repetitive electronic beep that grows more intrusive the longer someone remains nearby.
- The screen reflects approaching visitors but shows no normal image. Breaking the screen immediately stops the observation and silences the monitor, after which the otherwise empty room can serve as a temporary hiding place.
- Mokshi / Seer in Monitor (목시) is a disembodied eye: it only sees, relaying observations to the facility in real time. Its pulsing beep is audible before entry.

##### Feeding Floor / 6F (환자 식당층)
- The only level prominently marked with a visible `<6층>` sign. It consists of a long ward corridor beneath a false night sky, with patient-room alcoves along the sides and a locked service exit at the far end.
- Men, women, elderly patients, and children occupy the floor in hospital gowns, some attached to IV stands and others reduced to extreme emaciation. The moment a new outsider is recognized, every nearby patient turns and stares at them simultaneously. This collective gaze is the floor's immediate alarm state and must be broken, diverted, or absorbed through patient camouflage.
- Vacant posture, repetitive moaning, and primitive fear dominate; purposeful hiding, communication, and escape distinguish the sane minority.
- Before feeding, patients sit or stand in ordered clusters; afterward, blood drenches walls and floors while empty gowns lie neatly apart from remains. Cleanup restores unnatural spotlessness.
- The far service door is locked and difficult to force without alerting the facility. Janitor-Nurses carry the appropriate key during their cleanup rotation, making the interval after a feeding event the safest opportunity to leave the floor.
- Tranquilized Patients (6층 환자들) have suppressed higher cognition; one procedure uses invasive treatment through the ear canal while conscious. Screams and deaths may prompt only primitive terror.

**Gourmand Predator / Backwards-Speaker**
- A fabricated feeding subject deployed to the sixth floor on a schedule. It moves inverted on massively overdeveloped arms while thin legs remain raised above the torso and function as long-range striking limbs; its head has been replaced entirely by a single oversized mouth that constantly licks and smacks its lips.
- It announces hunger and intended prey through sentences spoken in reversed or distorted order, then attacks by whipping its legs across the corridor in broad horizontal sweeps. Its arrival marks the active feeding phase.
- During feeding, recognition obeys the camouflage rule above.

**Janitor-Nurses**
- Silent humanoids in nurse uniforms with a clean round hollow where the face should be. They appear in pairs or groups after feeding events and perform janitorial work with precise routine: scrubbing blood from walls and floor, collecting or folding abandoned gowns, and removing visible remains.
- They ignore tranquilized patients and generally ignore visitors who remain convincingly indistinguishable from them. They do not attack without a behavioral trigger, but obvious awareness, interference, or attempts to confront them break this tolerance.
- Each cleaning group carries access keys for the locked service areas, typically in a uniform pocket. Their scheduled appearance makes them both a timer for the feeding cycle and the primary source of the sixth-floor exit key.

##### Patient-Room Alcoves
- Small side spaces connected directly to the sixth-floor feeding corridor and populated by the same tranquilized patients. They provide concealment but no alternate exit.
- An entrant hiding here must continue matching the surrounding patient behavior. Deliberate whispering, checking the corridor, preparing a weapon, or reacting normally to screams can distinguish the entrant from the ward population when staff pass.

##### Director's Engagement Floor
- Open corridor-and-atrium area used as the Director's principal confrontation space, identifiable by shattered windows, broken ceiling panels, scorched walls, pulverized plaster, and a heavy acrid smell layered over the usual disinfectant.
- Wide sightlines and limited cover strongly favor the Director. His short-range movement is fast enough that he can cross a room during a momentary lapse in visual attention, making ordinary distance unreliable once he begins an engagement.

**Gangbuk Hospital Director (강북 병원장)**
- A seventy-four-year-old elderly man in a physician's white coat. His upper face appears almost completely ordinary, but the lower jaw hangs unnaturally to the level of his sternum, allowing the mouth to open into an enormous cavity while he continues speaking and observing with clinical composure.
- Opening the mouth is the clearest attack cue. Jaw closure erases anything fully enclosed from the local physical state rather than biting normally: flesh, limbs inside untouched clothing, wall sections, open air, and incoming projectiles or force can vanish.
- He moves with extreme short-range speed and may cross an entire room between moments of attention. Objects jammed into the mouth during opening or heavy blows against the hanging lower jaw can interrupt closure, but ordinary attacks do not solve the underlying problem.
- Harmful objects or effects forced past the jaws remain in his stomachless mouth or throat until expelled and can damage him internally.
- He treats the sixth-floor population as research stock and evaluates successful experimental results with genuine professional satisfaction. His own altered mouth and taste are regarded not as deformities but as superior sensory organs capable of reading the fundamental nature of whatever he consumes.
fields.entities:
##### False-Sky Resident
###### Jellyfish (해파리)
- Luminous entities drifting beneath the false night sky above the sixth floor and deeper hospital spaces. Their presence is consistent with the soul-jellyfish manifestations found throughout other Hospital facilities.
- They provide a dim blue ambient light and remain visually detached from the immediate feeding cycle. Their exact relationship to Gangbuk's taste research is not externally obvious, but prolonged direct observation should still be treated as hazardous.

강북 특설병원.title: Gangbuk Special Hospital (강북 특설병원)

fields.identity:
- A god-like river anomaly manifested as vast submerged fleshspace and a personified deep core. River, territory, residents, generated anomalies, and core are one entity.
- It genuinely answers prayers with effectively unrestricted scale, interpreted through its own generative process. Demonstrated output can create world-ending conditions.
- Acquisitive by nature: it collects people, abilities, behavior, memories, possible futures, and even unrelated anomalous techniques, reproducing or incorporating them into later encounters.
fields.entry:
- Direct River Crossing: a sufficiently anomalous section of the river surface can form a traversable membrane leading downward into the Outer Fleshways.
- Bridge Ritual: bridges leading toward small island parks can act as entry points when crossed with deliberate intent. Keeping the right hand on the railing and continuing forward produces increasing vertigo and nausea; at peak disorientation, closing the eyes and continuing without reopening them completes the transfer into the Riverside.
- Midnight Reopening: at exactly 00:00, locations previously used for entry can reactivate. Running water begins producing an unnatural humming sound, and the prior incursion point becomes capable of transferring entrants into the interior again.
- Entry is not limited to unusual-looking locations. The surface river, bridge, island park, and surrounding public space can remain completely ordinary until the transfer condition is fulfilled.
fields.notes:
##### Surface Incidents and Information Exposure
- Surface activity does not require physical emergence of the fleshspace. The Riverside can produce urban-legend-like incidents through ordinary city environments, particularly deaths involving sealed spaces, household devices, or circumstances behaving according to folkloric rather than physical causality.
- It can also externalize anomalous lure material. One recurring form resembles an irregular honeycomb-like mass with the odor of burned human remains; prolonged proximity or handling produces increasingly strong self-destructive impulses.
