Its distorted speech deliberately halts and breaks into separated syllables, growing more agitated as control fails. Neither its broadcasts nor the scattered notes are inherently safe instructions.
- Its most severe attack erases a targeted student's existence, not merely their life. A disappearing companion may have suffered permanent erasure; destroying the nightmare will not restore them.
- Conventional physical attacks are poorly suited to the ghosts, and civilians have no reliable direct combat solution. Anomaly-derived psychic abilities can affect them; holy or sanctified force is especially effective, rapidly destroying many. The Master is also vulnerable to anomaly-derived and holy power.
- Destruction of its hunters drives the Master from indirect hunting to open defense. It may replace the route with an infinite corridor: the identical segment repeats both ways, without rooms, exits, or geometric variation, until projection control is forcibly broken.
- King Sejong Statue: a massive animated bronze statue deployed outside or around the building as a heavy combat asset during this escalation. It marks open confrontation with the controlling intelligence rather than routine ghost hunting.
- Continued loss of the ghost screen and structural control can force the Master to intervene personally. Its predator dignity is fragile: direct pressure can provoke terror, desperation, hostage-taking of surviving students, threats, and attempted flight from the collapsing projection.
- Civilians should avoid individual triggers, use notes cautiously, and survive until destabilization instead of confronting ghosts. A deliberate clear uses effective counter-anomalous or holy force to strip away the ghost screen, anticipating loops, the statue, and hostages.
- Secure surviving hostages before terminal pressure, prevent the Master's escape, and confirm its destruction. Death ends the current projection completely and is the only confirmed way to end the tale permanently; escape lets the phenomenon recur at another school.
- At its death the school cracks, bleeds from fissures, and disintegrates section by section before darkness consumes the remainder. Immediately seek a viable exit as it falls apart. Surviving victims return to the real side; return to sleeping bodies at full disappearance should not be relied on while physical escape remains possible. Previously erased people never return.

광기로 점철된 성당.keys: Madness-Steeped Cathedral, Beelzebub's Domain, 광기로 점철된 성당, 바알세불의 권역, Madness Steeped Cathedral, 타락한 성당

fields.identity:
##### Occupied Sacred Site
- A religious-class site infestation: Beelzebub, Great Demon and Lord of Flies, seizes an existing Catholic cathedral and transforms it in place into its own body. This is a real consecrated site, not a new pocket dimension or an entity born from the building.
- The recorded target is strategically significant, suggesting deliberate selection; the criterion and any larger purpose remain unknown even after the demon dies. Left undisturbed, corruption spreads beyond the grounds, incorporating the surrounding environment.
- The domain's main danger is a private conversion attempt: Beelzebub seeks willing belief and participation in its restoration. Vermin and combat defend that purpose. Its body and the occupied building are physically continuous, so damaging the interior directly wounds the demon.
fields.space:
##### Approach and Physical Domain
###### Outer Corruption Perimeter
- A sustained red sky and circling crows mark the boundary. Grass, hedges, and trees wither; glowing crimson-eyed black rats hide below, black snakes coil in dead branches, and flies and carrion beetles saturate the air. These are demon-aligned extensions, scouts, and environmental hostility, not ordinary wildlife or independent anomalies.
- Physical entry needs no invitation. Crossing the perimeter exposes entrants to malicious domain pressure and hostile vermin, intensifying toward the building. Civilians are already unsafe here; withdrawal should evacuate the surrounding district as the radius expands, not merely retreat beyond church grounds.

###### Entrance, Nave, and Organ-Walls
- The front door looks superficially like a cathedral entrance but belongs to Beelzebub's body. Inside, thick black bristles cover surfaces; floors resemble segmented abdominal armor, walls layer chitin with organ tissue, and sacred architecture is reproduced in fly anatomy. Stained glass shows swarms covering the world.
- Strikes against doors, walls, floors, ceilings, or dividers split tissue, spray ichor, and make the building flinch. Deeper partitions enclose Familiar reservoirs. Systematic room-by-room demolition both hurts Beelzebub and removes the environment supporting its servants.
- Baal's Familiars are pug-sized, obese houseflies, proper retainers distinct from the ordinary swarms. Breaches release aggressive waves; accumulating damage opens deeper reserves. Demolition simultaneously provokes and depletes this defense.
- The underlying consecration survives the overgrowth, making strong holy effects exceptionally efficient. Holy fire consumes demonic tissue and entities without ordinary spread into unaffected material or the same smoke hazard, progressively easing corruption pressure as it cleans.
- Broad sacred-flame waves or expanding barriers can annihilate ordinary swarms and entire Familiar formations while leaving protected allies unharmed. Prepared combatants can clear the grounds and systematically burn or demolish interiors to weaken the demon directly.

###### Hall of Corruption
- The central sanctuary, especially the former altar, is the most transfigured area and the physical audience chamber. Beelzebub appears in lord-form: humanoid with a fly head, disproportionately small crown, long bristled forelimbs, and low decaying voice. Wiping its compound eyes with a forelimb while speaking gives it an incongruously human gesture.
- It controls the spreading field, swarms, Familiars, and Fly Kingdom personally. The Fly Throne anchors its selection of one visitor, generally the strongest or most useful, for a private subjective audience.
- Companions see about three seconds of blank, unresponsive staring while the chosen visitor experiences minutes. Brief outward duration does not make this interaction harmless or incomplete.
fields.rules:
##### Fly Kingdom and Temptation
- The target enters a barren black wasteland swept by winds of trillions of flies. A distant fortress is a mountain-like mass of dead flies. Beelzebub controls the whole presentation, throne included. There is no ordinary door or navigational exit; outright rejection or direct disruption collapses the audience and returns the visitor to the cathedral.
- Its conversion follows a deliberate progression tailored to real fear, spiritual uncertainty, prior anomaly exposure, and the desire for protection or knowledge:

1. **Discredit the accusation.** It claims to be the old sun god Baal, branded a demon by a victorious rival religion. Moral condemnation becomes alleged political or theological slander.
2. **Isolate the chosen audience.** The private Fly Kingdom removes immediate social resistance and presents itself as revelation.
3. **Establish credibility.** Genuine, limited supernatural perception can identify metaphysical facts such as a target having crossed death or returned from an afterlife state. This real insight is used to lend equal credibility to later promises; it is not omniscience.
4. **Name a real fear.** Old religious structures, it argues, cannot meet the present age of anomalous horror. Humanity needs a protector able to oppose what conventional faith cannot.
5. **Request restoration.** It wants more than worship: the target must perform a rite and use their own power to release it from demonic condition. Restored godhood supposedly lets it raise a new sun and shield humanity from supernatural terror.
6. **Stage proof.** Black flies part to reveal blue sky and golden sunlight. The same being appears as Sun-God Baal, a powerful, majestic figure in celestial robes and a noble, elaborate crown, with eyes presented as seeing the future. The divine form is a persuasion asset, not another entity.
7. **Offer secret knowledge.** It knows something of other major anomalies, including the Black Tower, whose image it can reproduce in flies. Depth and reliability are uncertain; possession of information does not validate the larger bargain.

- The offer is fundamentally deceptive. Insight is narrower than claimed, salvation requires empowering the entity presently consuming a cathedral and surrounding it with malice, and its connection to human sacrifice contradicts its claim of mere unjust slander.
- Civilians should avoid negotiations, demonstrations, and bargains rather than try to out-argue it. The conversation makes cooperation look morally reasonable. A prepared, mentally resilient target may deliberately let the attempt progress far enough for its mythic failure condition, then reject the entire bargain; partial negotiation does not fulfill complete rejection.
fields.survival:
##### Failure Window and Aftermath
- Conclusive failure of the completed temptation is a metaphysical defeat, not just wounded pride. Beelzebub loses power and composure together, becomes physically unstable, vomits ichor, and opens a brief decisive vulnerability window.
- The Fly Kingdom collapses and the target returns. The divine display sheds like an insect molt; the wounded, enraged fly-demon reappears in the Hall amid erupting swarms.
- The strongest clear combines physical siege with this deliberate temptation failure. Apply terminal force immediately on its wounded return, before recovery; holy or sanctified attacks are especially effective. Reliable clear requires complete destruction, not mere expulsion.
- Death ends active demonic occupation, but the real cathedral and physical consequences remain. Purify the site, recover human remains, and perform appropriate rites; corruption may have distorted remains beyond ordinary handling. Cleanup does not resolve why this particular consecrated strategic site was targeted.

광기로 점철된 성당.title: Madness-Steeped Cathedral / Beelzebub's Domain (광기로 점철된 성당 / 바알세불의 권역)

fields.identity:
##### Storefront and Game Frame
- A mobile pocket-dimension café parasitizing recently vacant second-floor shops in busy commercial districts. Prize signage and the appearance of a new entertainment business lure customers; the Manager opens temporarily and relocates rather than occupying one fixed address.
- Visitors walk upstairs without tickets, payment, reception, or staff. Motion switches on a single old-streetlamp-orange light above a black ebony counter in an otherwise dark interior. Ordinary price information and commercial equipment are absent. A corded telephone behind the counter triggers the welcome broadcast; a rule sheet follows, the dark rear door unlocks, and crossing it enters the larger game space.
- Perception impairment begins on entry and strengthens when visitors accept the attraction's game frame. Monsters become animatronics, victim records props, transfer elaborate construction, and danger mere concept. Even anomaly veterans may feel only distorted suspicion. Clarity returns outside or when a sufficiently stronger anomalous effect breaks the impairment; recognizing the storefront before acceptance is the safest decision point.
- The establishment turns terror, humiliation, injury, and death into recorded footage for non-human buyers, and failed customers into living meat, partial bodies, personality-bearing material, or other products. Fixtures and staff are property; participants can forfeit their bodies.
- The game is genuinely clearable. A legitimate completed run is valuable content, so the Manager honors release. Its rules are enforced by his domain control, not inescapable physical law; overwhelming force can bypass puzzles or destroy the venue, but provokes enforcement rather than counting as legitimate completion.
fields.rules:
##### Rule Sheet
**Rules to Know Before the Game**

1. Investigate the starting room, learn the theme and hints, and find the escape. The limit is at most 72 hours; exceeding it makes your body this establishment's property.
1-1. A forfeited body cannot be returned by any means.
1-2. It may undergo severance, torture, destruction, and similar treatment. You cannot protest.
2. Do not damage our property. It is more precious than your inferior body; even your entire body cannot compensate for damage.
2-1. We collect harshly from vandals. Even death will not let you escape.
3. Injury and torture during the game are natural. You cannot protest; protest brings punishment.
3-1. Some puzzles can only be cleared through injury. We hope you enjoy them.
4. Injury to staff will without fail be collected upon. All your body parts will not suffice, so look forward to it.
4-1. Staff attacks for game progression are natural. You cannot protest.
5. There is no midway abandonment. It makes your body our property. Please do not ruin our game.
5-1. Attempted self-destruction also counts as abandonment; ruining the game is harshly punished.
6. Illegitimate clears bring corresponding bodily sanctions. Please do not ruin our game.
7. Filming is absolutely forbidden. Appropriate punishment and damages will without fail be collected.
8. We accept no responsibility for contact with other participants.
9. Outside food is forbidden for a more appropriate experience. Bringing it halts the game; you bear heavy responsibility for interruption.
10. Game over makes your body our property.
11. We accept no responsibility for death during play. Corpse-disposal costs are billed to your family.
12. Have an enjoyable game.

- The asymmetry is intentional: staff attacks are service, self-defense against them a customer offense. Timeout, abandonment, game over, and other disqualifications forfeit living bodies; staff injury and property damage bring additional retaliation and compensation claims.
fields.space:
##### Industrial Game Space
- The current theme is a rusted multi-floor nuclear or wartime facility: submarine hatches, pipes, tanks, control equipment, peeling paint, and sparse horror-house lighting. Progression runs 1F → 2F → 3F → final exit.
- The Manager designs theme, layout, hints, case files, staff, punishment, processing, and impairment. During pursuit, a just-used corridor can become a dead end or an alternate route open to divert players toward staff and away from resources. Directional moans and staff sounds herd them around keys, puzzles, and exits; a mental map becomes unreliable.
- Planted warnings are mechanically meaningful but deliberately look like cheap amateur horror props. This and impaired perception encourage dismissal. Search each area fully before crossing progression doors; lost access can mean missed necessities.

###### 1F: Equipment Rooms and Case Files
- Dark machinery rooms, hatches, pipes, tanks, and detached panels limit sight. A dried blood trail reaches a control-room side area with broken drawers, research-like papers, and an artificial diary memo: the final exit is on 3F or above, its key was lost on 2F, and the writer fears becoming a Thing.
- Elsewhere, a four-digit safe has a separate code hint. Solve it legitimately or break it and incur property enforcement. The early Case-File Compendium combines accurate hazard information with the Manager's display of failed-customer products:

1. **Jo Minsik**, male, 21, soldier on leave with a friend: reached 3F bleeding. Things tracked the blood, removed his limbs, and ate his organs; revived as head and ribcage, he was sold. His final complaint: he had already cut off a finger—how much more did the puzzle want? The Manager says he should have cut more boldly and charges spilled-blood cleaning at about one family member. Sacrifice can be substantial, not symbolic.
2. **Song Ingeun**, male, 27, office worker accompanying his younger sister: hid her and made decoy noise. The Thing understood, ignored him, and pursued her; his return to protect her led to capture. His melted body retained personality and was sold in bottles; enough combined bottles reproduce personality fragments. Staff interpret obvious bait and intent.
3. **Lee Suji**, female, 8, student with family: screaming and crying, she was eaten. The Manager dismisses it as failure to stay quiet; disobedience earns no mercy.
4. **Nam Jeonghee**, female, 19, student on a date: took the 2F key and ran. Detected breathing drew Things from multiple directions; they tore her apart. The Manager says to search thoroughly for missed items and hints before progression doors.
5. **Kim Inwoo**, male, 25, freelancer with a friend: fought a Thing with a steel pipe, was caught and processed. The Manager's sole concern is the staff-injury violation. Injected with additional ingredients and sold as cooking material, he receives high Monster Customer ratings for his screams while eaten alive.

- These are genuine records under their cheap presentation. Blood, breath, crying, and shouting expose players; defensive violence invites severe retaliation, and failure may continue through revival or commercial processing beyond death.

###### 2F: Escape Key and Patrols
- Patrol density increases. The normal escape key is commonly placed where retrieval crosses patrol sightlines. Running with it can draw multiple Things through breathing alone.
- Civilian progression calls for full searching, quiet movement, breath control, no exposed bleeding, and no unnecessary repeat crossings. Combat-grade visitors can fight through, but killing staff can draw dozens from different directions and escalate the game into conflict with the Manager.

###### 3F: Sacrifice and Exit
- Rusted architecture continues past tall vertical fuel or heating-oil tanks. Injury puzzles require major bodily sacrifice; at least one needs a severed body part rather than token blood or a minor wound.
- The legitimate solution uses the participant's own body. A Thing's severed limb might satisfy the physical mechanism, but acquiring and using it violates staff-protection rules separately.
- Rupturing tanks releases large gravity-fed oil flows, allowing venue destruction at the cost of property enforcement. This is not puzzle completion.
- The final exit ends 3F progression. The necessary key, completion within 72 hours, and absence of disqualifying failure permit a legitimate clear and return to the entrance side; no legitimate withdrawal exists midway.
fields.entities:
##### Staff and Manager
###### The Thing
- Twisted, half-melted humanoid masses leak fluid and move with wet, heavy steps. Their irradiated-mutant look belongs to this theme, not necessarily their underlying nature.
- Blood scent, breathing, and sound guide them. They intelligently reject obvious diversions. Their speed closely matches a human sprint, so straight pursuit does not gain distance; the Manager's spatial editing supplies the eventual corner.
- Staff patrol individually but collect in swarms of dozens after injury, approaching from multiple routes. The Manager may replace or reintroduce them through off-screen paths while he retains control. They are predators and employees, protected as such by the rules.

###### Manager and Personal Domain
- A suited male humanoid with eyes and lips grotesquely enlarged like resized photographic features. His retail politeness and false professionalism cover pride and volatility. He can interrupt perception with spaced-out comments responding to participants' actual conversation; criticism provokes disproportionate hostility, while staff casualties or property destruction bring rage and speech broken into separated syllables.
- Heavy disruption draws him out rather than automatically killing him. Black spatial mire can remove the floor under targets, dropping them into a lightless personal domain without visible walls, floor, or stable orientation. His territorial power is strongest here; defeating staff does not confer safety against him.
- Confirmed neutralization uses a stronger external anomalous domain to completely overwrite his ownership. Spatial powers dependent on that territory then fail, allowing physical subdual or destruction. Powerful intruders can break doors, kill staff, and burn the fuel infrastructure to force this confrontation, but destruction alone neither releases them nor defeats him.
fields.notes:
##### Monster Customer Network
- Buyers beyond the café independently purchase footage and victim-derived goods: revived partial bodies, bottled personalities, and living food. Previously sold victims may remain there after the current venue is destroyed.
- The Manager can contact these customers and reveal a route to their side. Recovering that information remains strategically important: destroying the storefront, game space, or even the Manager neither erases the network nor automatically recovers its victims.

기괴한 방탈출 카페.title: Strange Escape Room Café (기괴한 방탈출 카페)

원숭이 꿈 괴담.keys: 원숭이 꿈 괴담, 몽키가든, Monkey Dream

fields.identity:
##### Abduction and Railway Cycle
- A subway abduction anomaly wearing the Japanese internet tale of the Monkey Dream: a narrator repeatedly dreams of riding with dazed passengers, a broadcast announces the station occupants' deaths, monkeys massacre them, and the final recurrence warns, "Next time, you will not escape." Here abduction is physical, not dreaming.
- A vampire colony has seized the anomaly. Its monkeys and Conductor now use the massacre structure to hunt humans and supply blood.
- Anomaly-detection GPS marks an active point in an otherwise normal metropolitan station as a RED DOT. Approaching it causes implausibly thinning crowds, cold air, and vanished ambient sound; crossing instantly transfers victims to the dark platform. Commuters may enter accidentally: "I was about to take the subway when the scenery suddenly changed." Withdrawal before reaching the point can avoid abduction.
- Train arrival, the Conductor's massacre announcement, killing, and departure repeat on a railway schedule. Intervals between trains are safest for moving or communicating. Functioning station payphones connect outside only then; outgoing calls display `[□□□□□□□]`, a live distress clue. Report the station name.
fields.space:
##### Railway and Hunting Force
###### Dark Platform and Internal Stations
- Unlit, nearly silent platforms are covered with broad patches of dried black blood. Multiple internal stations absent from ordinary metropolitan maps imitate restrooms, information booths, shops, and stairs, all deserted. No staircase reaches the surface; there is no normal station exit to reality.
- Do not voluntarily board. Those already aboard can get off at the next stop and hide away from doors and expected monkey movement, then act during the interval.
- Dazed Passengers are ordinary victims sitting or standing blankly with little resistance even during slaughter. This condition is neither instant nor universal: newly taken people may still run, hide, leave at stops, call outside, and time their actions.

###### Train / Carving Station (도려내기 역)
- Arrival uses the ordinary announcement, "The train is now arriving." Cars resemble an abattoir, strewn with blood, organs, minced remains, dismembered bodies, and partial corpses. Some monkeys remain between stops, mutilating or playing with bodies.
- The train is an anomalous imitation, requiring neither realistic driving nor normal infrastructure. Inter-car doors can be forced, but after departure the railway behaves as a closed rotating circuit; ordinary travel cannot return home.
- "Next station, Carving. Carving Station." Internal station broadcasts correspond to the monkeys' work in the massacre cycle.

###### Vampire Monkeys
- At least twelve armed monkeys, with grotesquely bulging forward-facing eyes, vertical feline pupils, and about a hundred curved blade-like fangs. They carry knives and other cutting implements, grin, laugh `"Kihihihi"`, play with severed heads, and deliberately mince living victims. Dismemberment, mutilation, and draining serve both recreation and colony supply.
- Their fusion with the tale may disrupt ordinary vampire-detection effects without removing vampire weaknesses: garlic dissolves flesh like strong acid, holy power burns, and crosses, silver, and equivalent counters work. Once this protection is overcome, they can be killed like ordinary armed animals. Heavily outmatched survivors may panic, discard weapons, trample one another, and flee through the cars.
- Direct combat without appropriate vampire counters is unfavorable.

###### Conductor and Route Authority
- A Vampire Monkey in full railway uniform, normally the only one able to speak human language. It schedules the train, oversees killing, and delivers harvested blood to the hidden colony terminal. Its polite service announcement is: "We will now begin carving out the customers in the station."
- Killing it does not give a replacement driver access to its complete route; they remain on the circulating internal line. Its hat carries the vacant role's authority. Wearing it after its death transfers the Conductor role, restores full-route access, and makes the colony terminal a valid destination.

##### Colony and Blood Supply
- The terminal route emerges from enclosed subway space into a vast dark expanse. Beyond rocky mountains, dense pointed buildings form a compact vampire city with specialized facilities, organized logistics, armed personnel, and central leadership, not a makeshift refuge.
- Normally such a large population would betray itself through local disappearances and overhunting. Distant railway abductions conceal the settlement while feeding it: massacre and collection → large tanks in the train's rear cars → Conductor transport → dedicated uniformed reception, unloading, and security → Central Hall storage.
- Colony Ghouls are vampire-controlled servitors patrolling portions of the railway and settlement approaches, intercepting intruders beyond the Monkey Dream's own killing zones.
- Separate Colony Forces act as guards, cargo crews, patrols, and coordinated armed response. Automatic rifles and other firearms supplement vampire physiques; some individuals manifest bat-like wings. Blood and secrecy limit force size, but it is sufficient to defend the city, routes, and shipments.

###### Human Livestock Pens
- Restrained captives are repeatedly drained, with numerous extraction wounds. They are deliberately nourished to preserve body mass and long-term blood production rather than killed immediately.
- Prolonged captivity devastates them psychologically. Some cannot speak coherently, stand unaided, respond normally to humans, or recognize rescue.

###### Central Hall / Kenoorn (케노른)
- The central major facility receives blood and concentrates organization and defense. Under major attack, surviving vampires gather or retreat there.
- Kenoorn rules the city and is its highest confirmed authority, far stronger and more experienced than ordinary residents. Partial monstrous transformation grants powerful claws; blood-based explosive attacks violently repel opponents. He understands anti-vampire weapons and can immediately excise silver-contaminated flesh before damage spreads.
fields.survival:
##### Extraction and Two-Stage Clear
- Survivor extraction is distinct from full destruction: find conscious survivors in safe intervals and remove them without assaulting the colony. Exceptionally powerful holy artifacts or equivalent sacred abilities can tear a temporary spatial breach directly to reality, bypassing the railway's lack of ordinary exits.
- **First stage:** eliminate monkeys and Conductor to stop the active massacre and its immediate hunting force. The wider railway persists through its colony connection; displays may become `[Current Station: None]`, `[Next Station: None]`, and `[Doors Open: None]`. Use the vacant Conductor role to reach the hidden terminal as described above.
- **Second stage:** overcome organized colony resistance and kill Kenoorn. Loss of its central authority collapses the remaining settlement and supply system. Surviving humans can then return along the anomalous railway, and the Monkey Dream fully releases its victims into reality.

원숭이 꿈 괴담.title: The Monkey Dream (원숭이 꿈 괴담 / 몽키가든)

성자의 도시.keys: 성자의 도시, City of Saints, Saint's City

fields.identity:
##### City and Religious Control
- An apparently ordinary Korean city remains physically connected to the outside. Shops, convenience stores, motels, restaurants, nightlife, work, and shopping continue normally; peaceful streets conceal deep cult control. Ordinary travel permits entry and does not immediately prevent departure.
- The cult centers on a naturally occurring Saint, with a hidden vampire household behind its public religion: an unnamed Cult Leader, his wife, son Do-jun, and servant Daesik. Most believers are ordinary humans. Public cult and vampire structure overlap but are not identical.
- The distinction between worshipped "God" and Cult Leader is real. The Saint already possessed innate holiness when the Leader found him; the latter neither created nor understands it. Instead, he made himself protector and interpreter, controlling doctrine, organization, followers, and practical use of the sacred figure.
- Human followers recognize one another and circulate outsider information quickly. Workers, customers, and recruiters may watch without acknowledgment; aggressive evangelists ask religion, purpose of visit, and local acquaintances, sometimes revealing prior knowledge of the visitor's movements. Longer stays increase active attention.
- Remaining anonymous becomes difficult once noticed. Avoid disclosing lodging or contacts, extended recruiter conversations, and isolated places after identification. No visible supernatural threat does not establish safety; abduction and ghoul activity occur behind normal urban functions.
fields.space:
##### Distributed Sites and Captive System
###### Commercial and Recruitment Network
- Ordinary shops, lodging, restaurants, convenience stores, pedestrian traffic, and public evangelism form the surveillance network. Believers blend into customers, workers, and religious gatherings without supernatural transformation.
- The Leader divides people into believers and "unbelievers"; rejection or inconvenience can lead to abduction, imprisonment, blood harvesting, or ghoul conversion. His "teaching" may precede final disposition; those who do not accept or survive it can be drained, with blood or corpse passed down to subordinates.
- This social system survives independently of the household. Removing one vampire or even vampire leadership does not instantly make the city safe: followers may still identify or pursue outsiders and attempt to recover the Saint.

###### Abandoned Construction Complex
- A fenced cluster of unfinished outskirts buildings hides an operational base. Its underground level contains numerous ghouls and Daesik's waiting point for orders and nighttime assignments.
- Ghouls are former humans, often designated unbelievers converted at the Leader's order. Red-glowing eyes, attacks on sight, little or no meaningful speech, and lack of ordinary fear make them disposable predatory muscle around hidden facilities.

###### Human Livestock Facility / Nightlife District
- A residential villa holds numerous captives blindfolded and bound like animals, available as blood sources or individual family selections. The household maintains this supply separately from its public worship.
- Clubs still operate. The wife frequents a private room in one and is recognized enough for Daesik to enter under her authority. She and Do-jun exploit the captives; the son lives separately and orders women from the villa for personal use.

###### Public Worship Hall / Private Temple
- The public hall is distinct from the Leader's secret temple. Before large congregations he preaches through the Saint and displays his real power as benevolent proof. The Saint believes these outings help others.
- The private temple is outwardly ordinary, inconspicuous, and architecturally unextravagant, concealing its importance. Its lowest level holds the Leader's secluded quarters, accessible through blood-manipulated mechanisms; human women may be drugged and hypnotized there for feeding.
- The highest level isolates the Saint until the Leader wants his power or presence. Social dependency conceals the household's crimes and turns the supposed divine authority into a controlled asset.
fields.rules:
##### Blood as Orders, Information, and Access
- Household vampire blood carries encoded intent or information as well as nourishment. A vampire knowing a location can encode it in blood for another to learn by drinking.
- The Leader's Blood Bats carry remote commands like physical letters. Daesik normally waits hidden at his base, swallows the construct to receive its intent, and performs the assignment secretly at night.
- Blood can anomalously release a conventional lock when fed into its keyhole without the correct key. Daesik can also put his own blood in a human's mouth to cause temporary unconsciousness.
fields.entities:
##### Household and Saint
###### Cult Leader
- An unnamed male vampire, neither originally an ancient power nor part of a greater vampire succession. A chance encounter turned him; discovering blood-supported effective immortality, he adopted that existence. His fraud and manipulation skills predate finding the Saint.
- He built the cult around the man's holiness, then turned his wife and son, enjoying wealth, status, blood, and local political influence through the resulting family. He cites his wife's cancer as his reason for turning her.
- Publicly benevolent, privately an imprisoner, exploiter, manipulator, and creator of servitors. Stronger than the other household vampires and more skilled with blood, he extends claws and fangs, wraps himself in a dense blood aura, and weaponizes scattered blood offensively.
- Killing him can yield "Cult Leader's Crown of Thorns (교주의 가시 면류관)."

###### Saint
- An unnamed adult human male exceeding roughly 150 kg, with extremely pale porcelain-like skin and a round, childlike appearance. His mentality is markedly juvenile: trusting, innocent, direct, and emotionally like a young child.
- Innate holiness predates this cult and any association with established religion. Its unmistakable sacred presence is perceptible without belief and makes worship understandable to ordinary observers. It differs enough from conventional Christian holiness that the vampire Leader can stand near him without destruction.
- He means well, considers the Leader a caring father figure, and believes he is protected and taken out to help believers. Isolation prevents understanding of the hidden vampire system. He is an exploited asset, not automatically a hostile religious operator.
- Sufficiently abnormal external means can separate holiness from his body completely, removing the sacred presence and leaving him physically ordinary. The observed removal also produced severe memory loss and an abrupt shift to ordinary adult-like thought. This suggests a connection between holiness and arrested development; it is not an established explanation of his true nature.

###### Daesik (대식이)
- A male vampire created directly by the Leader, serving as disposable household labor. "Daesik" is his master's degrading slave-like name, not a respected family identity.
- Simple-minded, submissive, conditioned to obey, and acutely sensitive to stronger vampires' moods. He calls himself the Leader's close aide but is routinely mistreated by the family, accumulating deep resentment rather than affectionate loyalty.
- He creates ghouls from designated unbelievers at the Leader's order, maintains that force, abducts people, moves villa captives, and follows Blood Bat assignments. He is skilled at moving unnoticed and hiding in darkness; blood gives him temporary human incapacitation and receipt of commands or geographical knowledge.
- Once the Leader's authority breaks, his hatred of master and family can surface violently.

###### Wife and Do-jun (도준)
- The adult wife retains a youthful appearance through vampirism, with ordinary enhanced vampire strength, elongated claws, and fangs. Cult protection lets her enjoy nightlife freely. She participates in exploitation yet remains intensely attached to her son.
- Do-jun is comparatively young and inexperienced, treats Daesik as an inferior servant, and relies on his father's authority to threaten others and demand captives.
- Neither possesses the Leader's central religious authority; their household status derives from marriage and descent. Vampire family power, human cult control, and the Saint's holiness must not be treated as one interchangeable hierarchy.

성자의 도시.title: The Saint's City (성자의 도시)

불이 꺼진 관리국.keys: Bureau with the Lights Out, 불이 꺼진 관리국

fields.identity:
##### Blackout and Recurrence
- The Bureau's existing warning: "If the lights go out, trust nothing and run. The Bureau's lights do not go out."
- A recurring reality inversion in the Management Bureau's underground containment facility, most often during ordinary tooth-tree maintenance and tooth-fairy duty. In the confirmed onset, an opened gift box contains the accompanying senior agent's severed head; her headless body kills the victim. The event then restarts at the containment-floor elevator with the senior normal beside them. Once the anomalous phase begins, the lights fail.
- The ordinary corridor grid becomes a vast, completely dark labyrinth overlapping an apparent "Fake Bureau." People may possess coherent memories and faction knowledge validating that claim, but the event never establishes which Bureau is genuine. People, locations, affiliations, interpretations, and exits progressively lose credibility.
- Death-and-restart loops permit repeated known-safe actions; the event does not automatically counter them on later loops. A real name or registered codename exposes its owner through "the Database"; an unregistered alias can avoid recognition.
- Cells emit overlapping monstrous howls, pleas, screams, and machinery tearing people apart. Genuine captives cannot reliably be distinguished from bait. The PA repeats "Emergency situation. Emergency situation."
fields.entities:
##### Pursuers and Containment
- Double-door airlocks and ID-card locks secure cells along the expanded corridor network of sealed rooms and laboratory access. Retain the Bureau ID, use an alias, keep companions in sight, and never open cells solely because someone pleads for help.

###### Neck-Pulling Ghost
- System designation: "the woman who pulls your neck and makes your face white (목잡아당겨서얼굴하얗게만드는여자)." A pure-white-faced woman with an unnaturally long neck silently peers around corners. Changing direction can reveal her at the next corner; simultaneous appearances herd victims toward dead ends.
- Capture stretches the neck and whitens the face, creating another cheerfully hostile long-necked ghost. Personality, memories, speech, and knowledge survive conversion, letting former companions expose survivors' lies or concealed identities while joining the hunt.
- No physical attack is confirmed to harm or stop her. Avoid confrontation and dead ends. Her face and the hands emerging from anomalous windows share an unnatural pure white, suggesting one system rather than proving a separate origin.

###### Corrupted Senior
- Before manifestation in a loop, the accompanying senior behaves exactly as usual. Directly asking about the Neck-Pulling Ghost transforms her immediately.
- Her body blackens like unnatural shadow; eyes and spikes sprout and her head can detach. Familiarity remains beneath segmented speech: "W h a t a r e y o u d o i n g? I h u g g e d y o u s o w a r m l y." and "A r e y o u s t i l l l o o k i n g f o r t h e w i n d o w? T h e r e a r e L O T S o f w i n d o w s."

###### Escaped Cell Residents
- Tooth Fairies fly in swarms through open corridors, stripping a captured human's flesh and bone within seconds. Properly closed containment-cell doors stop them.
- Other contained anomalies can become roaming threats, including the Cow's Head (괴담 '소의 목') and a profoundly uncanny-valley primate.
- One locked cell holds the chained, suited Manager Cho Seong-choon. He sincerely believes he is a real-Bureau scout captured in the Fake Bureau ahead of "진공작전," a planned all-out offensive. His knowledge is internally consistent, not proof of which faction is real.
- He knows the warning Hyungbaek (흉백(凶白)) and recognizes or mentions Director Lee Dohyung, the sword corps, Manager Kwak Seongju, Spangdal, Danto, Jequion, Gorgodio, and Kurosuna.
fields.survival:
##### Confirmed Route Through Reality Layers
###### Research Lab / Authority Transfer
- A Bureau ID opens the lab. Gognija, the Containment Team's Research Chief, is fused into its display wall as a flesh-machine amalgam, drooling and ticking his head mechanically. Continued Cheongak Mary Hospital medication preserves residual mental integrity; speech is usually fragmented.
- Scanning him triggers: "Research team lead Gognija integrity check in progress... Critical condition confirmed... Bureau ID identified. Executing emergency protocol. Transferring the management team lead's authority."
- The transferred authority enables a RED DOOR along the lab's side during darkness. Gognija directs survivors to it and the Reality Re-recognition Device before total erosion.
- A friendly Pink Slime, ranging from fist-size to dog-size, moves to whichever door is threatened and merges with it to hold pursuers back. Breaching that barrier may splatter or destroy it.

###### Red Door / Reality Re-recognition Device
- Beyond the ID-locked red door: a faintly lit corridor, a long passage, stairs descending deeper underground, a single-button elevator traveling down, another short passage, then a final ID-locked door.
- Beyond stands machinery too vast to distinguish one device from interconnected machines. Presenting a valid ID produces "Checking... Permission verification." and "Activate the Reality Re-recognition Device? YES/NO".
- YES restores light and an apparently normal containment-floor state. This is another reality layer, NOT escape; no confirmed central-entity destruction method replaces progression through these layers.

###### Restored Layer / Final Window
- Routine resumes as though darkness never happened. The red door vanishes completely from the lab wall, staff deny anything was there, and tooth-fairy gift-box duty starts cycling again.
- Escalation eventually returns. At its climax one window appears exactly where the red door stood. Gognija can clearly scream "GO OUT THROUGH THE WINDOW."
- Return to the lab and enter only this window. White-out ends the immediate event through the sole confirmed true exit; the other anomalous windows kill. Restored lights, plausible memories, or the senior's familiarity do not establish release or resolve the real/Fake Bureau ambiguity.

불이 꺼진 관리국.title: The Bureau with the Lights Out (불이 꺼진 관리국)

fields.identity:
##### App Entry and Commercial Otherworld
- A mobile market-alley anomaly branded like a once-fashionable side-street district. Its vast maze holds stalls, shops, residences, back alleys, and deeper businesses, populated by non-human merchants and people assimilating into its commercial logic.
- Telephone-pole posters in an aging residential-commercial district advertise Route 16 with a QR code for a local event app. Launch it in the indicated area before full sunset: navigation threads narrow residential lanes, gaps, buildings, and apparent dead ends. After about sixteen minutes, ordinary light disappears, shop signs illuminate in sequence, and the city seamlessly becomes Route 16. The app confirms arrival.
- Permanent night uses market lamps, signs, gas lamps, old streetlights, and display windows. Commercial segments shift between traversals; a recorded stall district → familiar shopping strip → dark back alley is not a universal map or freely selectable sequence.
- Goods and services are real and sometimes useful. Prices can be memories, senses, body parts, people, future consequences, or other personal value; ordinary money may be meaningless.
- Lure Law progressively learns desires: displays move into the visitor's eyeline and merchandise, offers, and opportunities become harder to ignore. This erodes judgment through plausible reasons to stop and buy, rather than absolute mind control. Familiar business names become subtly wrong under scrutiny.
- Eye contact, a reply, disclosed information, or interest in stock can initiate a merchant's one-sided transaction and make refusal harder. Quiet, socially clean refusal without staring, insult, panic, or theatrical flight is often respected. Walk naturally with companions; do not disclose names, addresses, associates, occupations, weaknesses, or other information usable for later solicitation or trade.
fields.rules:
##### Ten-Thousand-Step Event
- The app is lure, navigator, counter, and the only confirmed orthodox exit mechanism. It must remain open, functional, and in the visitor's possession. Closing it, losing or destroying the phone, or an unrecoverable crash stops normal tracking and seals that route home.
- After entry it eventually activates a walking event starting at 10,000 and counting down footsteps. Each thousand-step threshold meaningfully changes segments, route choices, or commercial conditions. At zero, with the app still counting, exit navigation appears.
- Steps through alleys count; deep stores, storage rooms, salons, and other commercial interiors can suspend meaningful progress. Meanwhile passages continuously narrow, possibly below human width with no pedestrian exit. Progress does not require continuing deeper: loop or walk back and forth in a survivable segment to consume the counter.
- The pressure is competing demands, not an impossible counter: keep walking, resist increasingly personalized shopping, avoid constriction, and protect the device. Another active participant's usable phone might be recovered or forcibly obtained after loss, but this is a desperate, unreliable, unsafe substitute.
fields.space:
##### Segments, Shops, and Residents
###### Street-Stall Alley
- A crowded night market of abnormal food, curiosities, and body merchandise, under constant aggressive solicitation. Distorted humanoid vendors may touch a passerby and invite them to inspect valuables behind a stall with visibly no room behind it. Avoid studying their faces, decline quietly, and keep walking; a properly refused vendor may release the visitor and immediately solicit someone else.

###### Daily-Goods Alley
- Apparently familiar stationery, general, yarn, butcher, and other shops mingle usable-looking stock with anomalous goods. This normality is a strong lure.

###### Other Street Segments
- Meat-Themed Alley centers on restaurants, tastings, and consumption, repeatedly inviting misleading or involuntary food transactions. Prefer another available segment.
- Lighting Alley offers lamps, lit displays, and window products that burn viewers or damage sight. Passage is possible with eyes averted and natural behavior rather than staring.
- Old-Town Arcade is comparatively low-risk: an older shopping street, telephone poles and sparse signs under visible stars. It can supply repeated walking distance without entering more predatory areas.

###### Boutique Back-Alley and Salon
- The foul-smelling rear passage narrows nearly to shoulder width. Gas lamps illuminate repeated side doors; gaunt uniformed laborers with bent spines lean along walls, bloodshot eyes watch through cracks, and cigarette smoke has no apparent smoker. Do not continue into geometry closing around the body.
- Some watchers open doors for small addictive or desirable goods worth about a cigarette pack.
- A side door can lead through a storage labyrinth, secondary entrances, and workrooms far larger than its frontage, finally opening into a lavish tailor's atelier: chandeliers, brass, dark wood, gilt frames, green velvet, ivory mannequin torsos, and disembodied white-gloved hands at work.
- Mannequin clerks and hovering hands summon uniformed mannequin bodies and offer membership, fitting, employment, or escorted access deeper inside. Certain escorts lead to visitors reappearing as degraded laborers. Trespass, default, bad agreements, and other routes to Boutique ownership account for many of the back-alley workers.
- Humans are a normal trade commodity here. Valuable substitutes such as gold may sometimes be accepted; never generalize one shop's payment rules to another.

###### Back-Alley Slum / Goldfisheye Inn
- Failed visitors, dismissed workers, debtors, and people expelled from other businesses live here, increasingly treating deformity and transactional logic as ordinary.
- The Goldfisheye Inn turns an attempt at conventional safe lodging into its own trap; it is not reliable rest.
- The alley's broader population includes long-dead acquaintances, missing relatives, disaster victims, pedestrians from earlier decades, pupils of nonexistent schools, and adapted former entrants. Familiarity does not establish safety: some sincerely guide outsiders into transactions without considering themselves hostile.
fields.entities:
##### Recorded Traders
- Flayed Ox: a skinned bovine-like merchant displaying human eyes, oversized colored eyes, flesh-attached lenses, unfocused white globes, and other ocular goods. Interest starts a purchase and a gesture for payment. Accepted currency is undisclosed; aggressive price probing can deepen the transaction.
- Raw-Meat Butcher: a massive bloody figure with multiple working arms and a raw-meat head resembling a flayed bovine skull. Live portions of beasts, primates, humans, and tentacular organisms move in its display. Cattle-edible food is one known barter category. Repeated rejection makes its handling of stock more violent; avoiding prolonged inspection of its face reduces direct-aggression risk during negotiation.
- Dalkom Stationery: dense steel shelves in an old neighborhood shop, register at the rear. The six-armed keeper takes specifically dated memories rather than normal currency.
- Yarn-Shop Keeper: an elderly six-armed humanoid knitting among ordinary yarn and wet, blood-vessel-like filaments. Some purchases accept ordinary coins; proper payment may obtain use of the shop telephone.
fields.survival:
##### Payment and Irregular Boundaries
- Establish what a shop accepts before buying. Avoid irreversible prices in memory, senses, body, or identity where possible. Gold, reversed or anomalous coins, addictive goods, cattle-edible food, and other commodities can sometimes substitute, entirely at the particular merchant's discretion.
- Resident shortcut claims involving back doors, manholes, special shoes, limb payments, or easy exits are traps and must not displace the reliable 10,000-step route.
- Some deep shops have another main entrance facing outside Route 16's normal alley geometry. Its destination is not fixed or generally known; such boundaries are hazardous but can be exploited.
- One known irregular escape: enter such a shop without losing the return route, physically tether yourself to its interior with an available object, and use a working shop telephone to summon an external boundary-crossing anomaly. Hell Surcharge Taxi can be called at 666666 4444 8282. When it arrives beyond the main door, open it and move backward into the vehicle without turning around.
- This exception does not make ordinary shortcut offers trustworthy. The orthodox route remains preserving the running app, completing the counter in survivable alleys, and following the exit navigation at zero.

fields.identity:
##### Board Game and Guest Status
- A physical board game contains a fantasy-park otherworld: gaudy, old-fashioned attractions, mascots, parades, prize shops, brass-band music, and exaggerated family imagery. Enjoyment is enforced even through mutilation, death, and abusive mascot demands. Parties ignorant of the User Guide seldom finish without death, disappearance, or integration.
- The box, "Yukoae Theme Park! ~A Joyful Fantasy-Land Trip~", holds a capsule of colored pieces matching the required participant count. Each person draws one; color assigns team and starting territory. Withdrawal is unreliable once drawn. When the last required piece is taken and the board unfolded, everyone enters simultaneously.
- Entrants awaken in assigned zones with paper Fantasyland Admission Wristbands bearing three empty stamp slots. This is recognition as a legitimate guest, not decoration.
- To clear, every teammate must physically board three qualifying major attractions together, preserve the three stamped slots, and use the north exit. Carrying an unconscious teammate aboard counts. Fastest qualifying teams may receive a mascot-selected gift-shop prize, ranging from ordinary branded souvenirs to anomalous items.
fields.rules:
##### User Guide and Enforcement
The Guide has ten numbered articles; only the following seven are mechanically established.

1. Keep the Admission Wristband clean and intact. Loss, damage, destruction, or forced removal immediately revokes guest status: the person becomes an intruder, thief, criminal, or potential staff member.
2. Same-color teammates must stay together, within approximately five meters outside active attraction boarding/riding. Near the limit a thin red leash-like cord appears and tightens; exceeding it strangles. Closing ranks removes it.
3. Crying, wailing, screaming, and intense negative displays do not suit the park and are forbidden.
4. Theme and ruling mascot define each zone; the mascot's absolute territorial authority overrides ordinary park logic.
5. Changed mascot design and environmental color mean a new territory. The previous mascot cannot exist there or follow across its boundary.
6. Countless observing eyes remember guest behavior.
7. Cheer parades joyfully. Everything in them must be enjoyed without visible negative judgment.

- Music, rides, performances, and parades continue through casualties. Cursing, visible disgust, recoiling, and other serious negative reactions can instead freeze nearby machinery and silence music. After a brief counted pause, every guest, worker, mascot, and parade figure turns to the offender. Quickly ending the display can restore the performance; continuing brings punishment.
- Maintain controlled behavior, smile and clap lightly at parades, avoid prolonged mascot eye contact, and neither touch nor collect grotesque debris. Keep incapacitated teammates with the group rather than abandoning them.
- Cheerful attraction notices can state literal hazards. Real ride mechanisms exist—emergency buttons, panels, powered gates, service equipment—but a ride may suppress ordinary emergency stopping. Technical work is possible when mascot observation is avoided, not automatically safe.

##### Facilities, Staff, and Prize
- One silent, empty-eyed humanoid Attraction-Operator Mascot per ride stamps wristbands during boarding. Operators normally avoid direct attack but can report unusual conduct to the ruler.
- Zone-uniformed Information-Booth Mascots gesture routine directions to recognized guests. They are comparatively non-hostile until pressed for inappropriate, restricted, or member-only requests.
- Locker rooms, restroom backs, and service corridors have less routine mascot traffic and can support regrouping, treatment, or ritual preparation. Border gaps and backstage routes expose hollow decorative walls, dormant gates, and equipment; ordinary emergency panels may restore powered-down mechanisms.
- Gift shops award fast-clear prizes. Public-use phones and snack trucks provide access to mundane supplies such as food, water, torches, salt, and marshmallows.
- Good Friend: a soft plush prize activated with flame, about 100 ml water, one spoon of salt, one clean coin, and an object meaningfully tied to a friend. Completion permanently anchors an other-side mind in the doll. Materials from other anomalies can substitute but distort which "friend" responds.
- For standard departure, all teammates must still be recognized guests with three qualifying stamps each. Preserve wristbands and team proximity, then proceed to the north gate; neither a territory change nor Membership fulfills that condition.
fields.space:
##### Territories and Mascots
- Historical balance was red rabbit / blue dragon / yellow flower. Current runs overwhelmingly favor Magic Bunny, with Blue Dragon's waterpark peripheral and yellow territory surviving mainly as Flower Golden Resort. Borders sharply change pavement, brick, flags, signs, decoration, and imagery.
- The mural-sized Fantasyland Color Map near the Fantasy Train's rear exit/terminal records current borders. Near-monochromatic dominance means prioritize leaving that ruler's territory, not prolonged survival there.
- Narrow unowned border voids weaken both guest protection and mascot jurisdiction. Damage entirely inside such a gap does not automatically draw owned-zone enforcement and may open backstage or service structures. Decorative border archways can conceal removable cosmetic brickwork; crossing the exposed white-brick seam into another zone can stop pursuit.

###### Magic Bunny Fantasyland
- Red imagery saturates castles, tents, flags, Ferris wheels, carousels, coasters, Viking rides, and signs like a personality cult. Broadcasts call Magic Bunny the sole source of dream, fantasy, law, and pleasure; under stress they smear into overlapping speech that can induce dangerous panic.
- Magic Bunny is a giant red rabbit with spinning bloodshot eyes, forward-everting jaw teeth, and speech fixated on death. The current apex has actual mascot seniority: he has physically thrown Blue Dragon out of an active scene without the park deeming it improper.
- Favor starts with singing, waving, eating, holding something, or a warm hug. Compliance escalates toward severe self-mutilation, betrayal, and personally killing another guest; deep favor can make refusal physically difficult. This is accumulated debt and a route to party destruction, not a lasting alliance.
- Late hesitation brings rabbits clinging to attraction windows, staring or weeping blood while awaiting compliance. Losing favor removes practical protection and starts pursuit. An explicit late killing-demand refusal can unleash half-melted bleeding rabbits from painted surfaces, signs, fountains, and attraction mouths, faster than humans, biting, whipping pseudopods, and secreting flesh-dissolving fluid.
- Plausible delay or misdirection can buy time; crossing out of red immediately ends direct authority and blocks the swarm. Open refusal while staying inside is hazardous.
- His parades mix candy, fireworks, and confetti with organs, blood, entrails, and eyes. Spectators must keep smiling and cheering.

###### Blue Dream Waterland
- Tube slides, plume rides, pools, and shore boardwalks make this large blue waterpark one of the remaining places for relatively conventional ride clears. Milder does not mean safe.
- Blue Dragon wears an immaculate staff uniform, with button-like eyes and consistently polite posture. His private standards exceed the known Guide; he can execute a guest for an unlisted offense, then resume spotless calm. Intervening in punishment can simply add another offender.
- If pleased, he or an attendant may offer an Admission-to-Membership Wristband upgrade. Indefinite residence is its "reward": the north exit closes to the member. Politely decline and keep the arm out of reach.
- A trapped Membership holder can try the northwestern restroom-back path and restricted mountain trail to Flower Golden Resort. This changes hazards; it is not an exit.

###### Flower Golden Resort
- Surviving yellow territory centers on a hotel and promenade with a smiling yellow-flower motif, reached from northwest blue or valid inter-zone/backstage connections.
- Its mascot has a caprine plush silhouette, soft deep-yellow pile, featureless round black eyes, a broad muzzle, fractal golden-glass flowers on its horns, and a large golden bowtie.
- Hospitality, payment, employment, and propagation follow the separately defined resort system. Entering does not clear the main park.

플라워 골든 리조트.keys: Flower Golden, 플라워 골든, Flower Golden Resort

fields.identity:
##### Resort and Entry Vectors
- Flower Golden governs the yellow-territory sub-anomaly of Yukoae Theme Park: a fairytale hotel, promenade, spa, garden, and service complex. Smiling yellow flowers dominate glass-and-gilt façades, marble, gold, and ornate rooms. Hospitality, payment, room allocation, and employment are the main threats rather than rides.
- Park entrants arrive through a yellow piece at board-game activation or neighboring zones. Known routes include the mountain path northwest of Blue Dream Waterland and valid backstage/inter-zone connections. Older service gates may need emergency power restored.
- Park entrants retain wristband, team, and applicable zone rules. Legitimate stamps from qualifying yellow activities can count toward the parent park's clear, but leaving the resort and escaping Yukoae remain separate problems.
- Independent entry uses a Deluxe-room one-night promotional coupon with mandatory review. Blue Dragon may distribute coupons in the park. Accepting transfers the holder to the resort; after checkout a review is compelled. Meaningfully reading, hearing, or viewing propagated review material can summon another victim to the lobby, creating a stay → checkout → review → outside circulation → new stay loop.
- Review victims need not possess park Admission Wristbands. Their immediate obligations belong to resort hospitality, not automatically the three-attraction condition. Wristbanded victims, review-abducted humans, and anomalous non-human visitors all qualify as guests; payment, status, and compliance matter more than species.
fields.rules:
##### Guest Rules and Employment
- Ordinary operation starts around 09:00; front doors lock during closed hours. Standard payment is plastic Yukoae Coin. Human fiat money and ordinary precious metals are rejected.
- Resort Usage Rules require orderly reception behavior, no queue-cutting, loud disturbances, soiled lobby/corridors, unauthorized room invitations, or damage to room or resort property. Violations can cause anomalous accidents, punishment, restraint, or conversion. Interfering impulsively in discipline may itself violate the rules.
- A compliant dangerous non-human remains a legitimate customer; human guests receive no automatic defense against other guests. Food, gifts, and luxurious treatment are likewise not necessarily human-safe.
- Unpaid lodging can lead to a Resort Employment Contract. Its default compensation is lodging rights and one gift-shop item, with no conventional wage. Signing changes guest to staff, binds them to labor, and supplies no ordinary resignation merely because work is dangerous or unwanted.
- Staff Work Rules are separate and unstable: a short list can expand beyond thirty-seven entries without meaningful warning. Keep the current copy and re-read when circumstances change. The rules apply in staff rooms too; being off duty does not create a refuge.
- Living contracted staff remain conscious humans with their ordinary bodies and personalities. Death does not end the contract: Flower Golden can revive the employee with recognizable proportions, a yellow-flower mascot face permanently fused to the head, and a mascot resort uniform replacing their clothing. Converted workers cannot rest, refuse assignments, or leave normally.
- Preserve guest status and enough coins rather than treating employment as a lodging fix. Staff infiltration gives rescue personnel administrative access only at the cost of this bond; an independent anomalous exit capable of bypassing the contract is needed to avoid permanent employment.
fields.space:
##### Hotel Facilities
###### Front Lobby and Welcome Gift Gacha
- Gilded marble surrounds the central golden-flower emblem, front desk, lodger registry and pen, glass entrance doors, and golden Admission Wristband stamp beside the desk. Registration, rooms, payment disputes, upgrades, and employment offers begin here.
- A giant snow-globe-like Welcome Gift Gacha in the middle claims only good prizes. The gold-wrapped Special Prize upgrades its holder to a top-floor Suite. Participation is optional, never required for legitimate lodging; unclear benefits need not be accepted.

###### Facility Office
- Restricted to Flower Golden and recognized staff, not ordinary guests. Resort guidance, a self-writing pen, current Staff Work Rules, coin drawers, and an old wooden telephone provide administrative resources.

###### Guest and Staff Rooms
- Standard, Deluxe, and top-floor Suite accommodations commonly contain bottled-water refrigerators, crystal chandeliers, front-desk emergency bedside phones, and room-service intercoms. Contract workers receive comparable rooms without exemption from Work Rules.
- After hours, staff must not open merely for an employee or familiar voice, nor handle postcards, notes, or stationery pushed under the door.

###### Healing Golden Spa / Night Garden
- A glass skywalk links the hotel to the Spa, a fairytale glass-domed greenhouse of golden flowers whose treatments are delivered by "experts."
- Aromatic oils may list ordinary fruit together with human blood, bipedal-primate vascular fluid, and biological material from other anomalies. Luxury and hospitality claims do not make such products safe for humans.
- The Night Garden has golden-flower topiaries, reflective fountains, multicolored lit flower buds, and a central ceremony plaza.

###### Rear Service Wing / Staff Cafeteria
- Restricted backstage storage, freezers, cleaning, body handling, and room-service infrastructure lie behind the guest presentation. Human staff should enter only for a specific required task; authorization alone does not confer safety.
- The Staff Cafeteria is specifically provisioned for contracted humans, maintaining the labor force.
fields.entities:
##### Administration and Continuing Propagation
- Flower Golden has a caprine plush shape, soft deep-yellow pile, featureless round black eyes, broad muzzle, fractal golden-glass horn flowers, and a large golden bowtie. It controls guest acceptability, contracts, both rule systems, punishment, and dead-worker revival. Extended physical safety can coexist with steadily tightening institutional entrapment.
- Generic mascots are nearly identical yellow-plush, round-eyed staff with featureless voices and little individuality. Reception, gacha help, gifts, and doors share the same workforce as cleaning, room service, freezing, body disposal, security, restraint, and employee escort.
- Decline unnecessary upgrades, food, spa services, gifts, or gacha when consequences are unknown. The house treats compliance as sufficient customer legitimacy, not human welfare.
- Leaving a promotional stay does not stop its compulsory review from recruiting new victims. Treat the completed review as an active transmission vector and prevent its circulation. Park visitors must additionally fulfill their parent anomaly's escape requirements.

플라워 골든 리조트.title: Flower Golden Resort (플라워 골든 리조트)

눈먼 자들의 저택.keys: 눈먼 자들의 저택, Mansion of the Blind

fields.identity:
##### Exhibition and Contaminated Documentation
- An immense exhibition-mansion collecting sensory organs and philosophical interpretations of perception: seven above-ground floors and 7,221 below, with thousands of spaces extending from familiar galleries into structures no longer meaningfully describable to humans.
- It welcomes every entrant as a legitimate viewer under standards for non-human clientele. Human catastrophe from fees, devices, accommodation, or exits results from indifference, not ordinary predatory hostility. Its art and collection are genuinely valuable by its own standards.
- Meaningful written accounts—manuals, reports, memos, pamphlets, even warnings—can rewrite themselves into courteous exhibition invitations. Reading one makes the next meaningful movement or journey end at the Mansion, without a specific doorway. Companions and surroundings can disappear abruptly; simultaneous entrants may arrive in different floors or sectors.
- Documentation is itself transmission. After exposure, prepare before moving. The Mansion may also overwrite criticism, add corrections, or recast warnings as hospitality; statements technically true for its intended clientele are not reliable human safety advice.
fields.rules:
##### Free Hour and Admission Collection
- The first full hour is genuinely free. Guide Staff do not collect merely for presence during it. Use this reconnaissance window to identify the floor, route toward the grand staircase, and temporary concealment instead of touring deeper exhibits.
- Afterward, bodily admission falls due in recurring installments. Money, valuables, bribes, and non-biological substitutes have no payment value. Eyes are overwhelmingly the first collection; later rounds can take limbs, tongue, ears, or other parts.
- Collection is precise: Staff remove the part, close or treat the wound, and fit a temporary correction/rental device so viewing can continue. Initial eye collection is survivable with the usual sight replacement. A paid viewer is deprioritized until the next round.
- Staff circulate and collect on physically reaching an overdue viewer rather than maintaining relentless pursuit of each debtor. Hiding can delay a particular encounter, never cancel debt.
- Correction devices genuinely imitate sight, hearing, touch, taste, or other senses. Some instead provide senses humans lack; their neurological effects are unsafe and unpredictable. Prefer only replacements necessary for an already lost human sense.
- Breaking Staff limbs, doors, exhibits, or fixtures counts as disturbance, theft, and property destruction, summoning additional units and liability. If collection is unavoidable, accepting a scheduled installment is generally less dangerous than triggering that escalation.
fields.space:
##### Navigation and Galleries
- European-style upper numbering is 0F–6F, with B1 onward below. Assuming the first visible level is "1F" risks missing the actual exit floor. All signs, floor labels, exhibit placards, lift controls, and most internal writing use a script without human linguistic cognates; arbitrary/anomalous-writing translation is needed for reliable reading, including the elevator lore plaque.
- The warm upper levels use candles, brass, gold, heavy drapes, upholstery, antique tables, ornate frames, and recognizable gallery architecture. Exhibits mix organs, biological structures, artificial perception, and philosophical treatments of emotion, gaze, or sensation; human-derived components also occur.
- Below, bronze darkness replaces gold warmth as architecture and art become biological, abstract, and increasingly incompatible with human thought. Thousands of floors make a downward search for a conventional bottom exit effectively suicidal.

###### Main Galleries and Temporary Cover
- The 0F–6F upper section is most comprehensible, but 0F itself is the entrance lobby rather than an exhibition floor. Occupied exhibition levels contain major themed halls; deeper work makes biological interpretation increasingly literal.
- Connecting corridors offer alcoves, heavy vases, sofas, and occasional ventilation access. Ducts, alcoves, low-patrol areas, and terrace rooms can hide a viewer briefly, not provide permanent safety.
- Window-like doors may conceal small hexagonal terrace rooms with sofas and low tables. Going beyond their exterior—or using any apparent window as escape—reaches thick black fog outside the Mansion's shell, with no reliable return inside and no return to reality.

###### Spiral Dual-Staircase / 0F Lobby
- The main hall's grand spiral dual-staircase passes a concealed intermediate landing with a doorway to 0F. Ordinary floor-counting can miss it; the floor does not join the standard stair network like upper exhibition floors.
- 0F is a silver-toned entrance lobby without ordinary exhibit halls. Cross it and use the stained-glass main gate, the only established regular human exit, returning to the real-world location associated with the original entry medium.
- Claims that any viewer may leave are semantically valid for the intended clientele. Marked/emergency exits generally are not human routes home; the particular 0F gate is what matters.

###### B1 Visitor Lounge
- B1 begins the darker, bronze-toned underground transition. The lounge has armchairs, vintage tables, and a working fireplace. Exhibition bans on eating or open flame relax here, making it the best known place for rest, food preparation, and fire-based work.
- Staff visit less often, but neither admission debt nor their access is removed.

###### Elevator, Front Desk, and Deep Tracts
- An antique brass-caged elevator reaches distant levels, but unreadable controls usually require summoning an in-cabin Guide to choose a destination. This practically guarantees close collection if payment is due.
- Somewhere in the Mansion, a Front Desk arranges long-term guest rooms. Guides can confirm it with simple yes/no answers, but it is not reliably near arrival. Residence merely adds collection cycles, not a solution to the time limit.
- At approximately B100 and deeper, surviving accounts fragment and anatomical/artistic categories fail. B105 records include perception through the wrong sensory organs and human-derived structures on skeletal or bone frameworks. Deeper exploration demands unavailable senses or concepts while worsening navigation.
fields.entities:
##### Staff, Viewers, and Collector
###### Guide Staff
- Automatic steam dolls combine docent, collector, surgeon, rental technician, corpse retrieval, and enforcement roles. A typical unit fuses giant spider with female mannequin: segmented upper body, eight gas-lamp-like facial lights, extremely thin articulated metal limbs, and jerking near-bipedal movement accompanied by long mechanical shrieks and rhythmic hammer impacts.
- Needle limbs excise parts while other thread-and-needle limbs close wounds and install rentals. Force can break individual limbs but invokes property enforcement. They are dutiful and courteous, not conventionally sadistic; human objections have no economic meaning to them.
- Head movements answer simple yes/no questions about nearby zones or services. Their limited knowledge does not make them omniscient navigators.

###### Converted Viewers
- Repeated fees leave long-stay humans missing eyes, limbs, tongues, or ears, with deteriorating correction devices. They crawl, breathe or sob instead of speaking, and may desperately seize passersby to be carried out. Their route knowledge and offers of guidance are unreliable.
- When a viewer permanently stops moving, Staff retrieve the body. Remains and harvested components may later enter the deeper collection.

###### Mansion Collector
- Internal lore exalts an owner sharing art, philosophy, and rare sensation. No physical manifestation is confirmed; a separate entity, absent owner, or personified curatorial system remain possible interpretations.

눈먼 자들의 저택.title: Mansion of the Blind (눈먼 자들의 저택)

fields.identity:
##### Activation and Assigned Roles
- A long-abandoned private English-immersion kindergarten on the town outskirts, surrounded by vacant-lot weeds. Before activation, dust and decay surround an incongruously intact entrance-hall pendulum clock.
- Participants must enter before 09:00. In the last seconds, the institution selects one Hangman, marked by a black rope-like ring around the neck, and assigns the rest as New Teachers. At the chime, the building becomes spotless, pastel, bright, and new-smelling; everyone scatters into random rooms and the announcer begins childcare staff training.
- Standard intake is about twelve: one Hangman and eleven New Teachers. At least two can activate it; fewer than two have no confirmed survivors.
- Hangman becomes a compulsory biographical word game. No legitimate role refusal, role exchange, or safe nonparticipation exists. New Teachers must help execute a colleague or accumulate penalties toward permanent employment. The victim is exempt from ordinary facility penalties while designated, but cannot move freely.
- Cheerful quiet persists without continuous pursuit. CCTV, workplace conduct, mandatory contribution, and the selected victim's expected death supply the pressure. No normal children ever appear, despite perpetual readiness for a school day.
fields.rules:
##### Faculty Rules and Penalties
- CCTV monitors every New Teacher; no blind spot is confirmed. Moving faster than a brisk walk, profanity, loud cursing, property damage, unauthorized stage entry, detectable lies to staff, and breaches of the current game rules immediately incur penalties. Rules apply throughout the facility unless explicitly relaxed.
- A violation slams a black book-like mass onto the face, adhering like molten tar. For about ten minutes the victim rolls or writhes while compelled to recite the Education Book. Do not touch someone undergoing this punishment.
- It dissolves into a pale iron-branded class designation on the forehead, such as Chick Class or Sprout Class, marking the accumulated penalty. Three cause immediate permanent conversion. "Education" continues until a proper teacher is formed, with no meaningful endpoint.
- Converted teachers are constantly smiling, professionally warm, rule-obsessed, and committed to a denial loop that the kindergarten is perfect, safe, accident-free, and wholly compliant. They do not display ordinary brainwashing distress.
- Keep penalties at zero where possible: even a "minor" violation counts, and silence does not avoid game grading.

##### Hangman Session
- Black ropes bind neck, shoulders, waist, arms, and legs, suspending the selected victim without immediately strangling them. Head and face remain mobile for seeing, speaking, and participating.
- A CRT displays a blank English word, usually about eight letters but variable. It is the single term best expressing the victim as a person, possibly a loaded character judgment.
- New Teachers raise hands and call English letters. Periodic hints assigned to blanks ask about the Hangman's private life: past jobs, fears, trauma, dead acquaintances, consequential decisions, concealed relationships, and other undisclosed history. Public reconstruction of the conscious victim's biography is part of the game.
- Correct letters fill blanks and detach corresponding body sections instantly, painlessly, bloodlessly, and without wounds, like dismantling a model. Parts stand upright near the stage, broadly progressing from feet and legs through hips, torso, arms, neck, then head. The sequence preserves speech for most of the game.
- The victim usually knows the hints best and, if willing, can explain history, direct choices, and distribute credit. Every New Teacher needs at least one correct letter by game's end; no contribution earns a penalty. Track credit and share viable guesses before scarcity produces coercion or rivalry.
- Completing the word briefly reconstructs an execution body on the gallows and physically hangs the Hangman. Afterward the separated condition resumes, not an ordinary restored corpse. One designated death is the normal successful cost.
